articles.title: Colin Kaepernick's Wife Surprised By How He's Handled Losing $150 Million
articles.summary: She admits she's surprised by it.
articles.body:
Former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick is estimated to have lost out on roughly $150 million after taking a knee for the national anthem in 2016.

Kaepernick last played in the league in 2016, when he began kneeling for the national anthem. The former San Francisco 49ers quarterback went unsigned a few years after leading his team to a Super Bowl appearance. Kaepernick likely lost out on a nine-figure contract.

"Kaepernick, in his physical prime at 29 and three years removed from leading the 49ers to the Super Bowl, went home and waited for calls from other teams," the San Francisco Standard reported.

"A decade later, he's still waiting — essentially blacklisted from the sport he loved after protesting police violence by taking a knee during the national anthem. For those acts of protest, Kaepernick was banished and deprived of earnings he estimates at $150 million."

Kaepernick has remained committed to his cause.

"I've been very focused on doing the work. I mean, I want to make sure we're doing it, moving things forward, having impact. But the other part is, there was a realization that I was being positioned as the sole figure to be able to represent the movement, and I need to create space for other people to step up and be leaders. I think of Ella Baker [a Black hero of the civil rights movement] — her work centered around, yes, we need strong leaders, but we need strong people collectively," he told The Standard.

He remains interested in an NFL comeback, though it's highly unlikely.

"Over the last 10 years, we have consistently reached out to teams, over and over again, knocking on every door possible, and that's shown up [publicly] in a few instances, the most recent one being 2022, the workout with the Raiders. For me, I want to make sure that at any point in time, if my door is knocked on, that I'm ready to go," he added.

Nessa, his wife, remains surprised by how at peace he is

Kaepernick's wife, Nessa, remains surprised by how he's handled losing out on a nine-figure, life-changing payday.

"In the 10 years since Colin @kaepernick7 began his peaceful protest, the personal sacrifice has been enormous. Because of the stance he took, he lost his NFL career, more than $150 million, and dealt with betrayal along the way. After everything it has cost him, I wanted to know how he's still been able to find joy and peace," she shared.

It's an impressive mindset for Kaepernick to have.

articles.title: Australian Star Point Guard Luke Paul Commits To Duke For 2027-28 Season
articles.summary: Australian guard Luke Paul has committed to Duke for its 2027 recruiting class.
articles.body: Jon Scheyer is at it again. Known for locking down elite talent, the Duke Blue Devils head coach made a major splash on the international trail by securing a commitment from one of the world's premier young recruits. First reported by ESPN, point guard Luke Paul has committed to the Blue Devils for their 2027 recruiting class. The 6-foot-6 Australian guard is highly regarded as a potential lottery pick in the 2028 NBA Draft. Paul delivered a standout performance at the U17 FIBA World Cup in Turkey with Team Australia. He averaged 15.4 points, 6.4 rebounds and 7.1 assists per game alongside his play with the Cairns Taipans. Not only is Paul a unique talent, but he marks the second commitment in the Blue Devils 2027 recruiting class. He will now join four-star forward Kager Knueppel in the program’s early commitments, with plenty of other top targets still in the mix. Knueppel is the younger brother of Charlotte Hornets guard Kon Knueppel, following directly in his brother's footsteps. Paul was named to the All-Tournament Team at the FIBA U17 World Cup over the summer, where future Duke teammate Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje took home MVP honors. By expanding his recruiting footprint internationally, Scheyer has secured two high-upside talents for Duke. While Scheyer has built Duke into a perennial power since taking over the program, a National Championship still eludes him. With consecutive elite recruiting classes and an influx of top international talent, pressure is mounting to see if they can finally get over the hump.

articles.title: How Did Tom Brady Learn To Say 'Meatball Sub,' And How Many Such Passes Did He Throw?
articles.summary: Tom Brady shared how he learned about the "meatball sub" phrase after calling Justin Herbert's
articles.body: When Justin Herbert threw a costly interception in the Los Angeles Chargers' loss to the Buffalo Bills last week, Tom Brady was more than blunt when he assessed the quarterback's errant throw. "There's a safety in the middle of the field. Poor awareness, poor decision, throws him a meatball sub," Brady said of Herbert's throw, which landed right in the arms of Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson. Brady's quote quickly went viral. FOX Sports' video of the quote generated over 300,000 likes on Instagram, while a handful of posts on X about Brady's comment garnered several thousand likes and views. But how did Brady learn about the term that's become popular on social media for whenever a quarterback throws a bad pass? In the latest edition of #AskTom, Brady let everyone know that his kids have helped keep him hip to popular social media vernacular. "Chill, chill. Relax. Everyone's got to remember, I've got three kids, OK? So, that should just point you in the right direction," Brady said when asked who told him to say "meatball sub." Brady's "meatball sub" remark was the second straight week that he said something on a broadcast that quickly made the rounds on social media. A week earlier, he called one of Dak Prescott's passes a "piss missile" in the Dallas Cowboys' victory over the Washington Commanders. Brady apologized for the "piss missile" comment in last week's edition of #AskTom. But he isn't apologizing for his "meatball sub" quote, although he admitted that some of his passes were meatball subs. "I threw a lot. I probably threw over 200 interceptions in my career. I would say somewhere between 25 and 50 [were meatball subs]," Brady said. "And, believe me, Coach [Bill] Belichick, he never let me forget those." That led Brady to express his appreciation for the coaching he got from Belichick over his career as he touched on that topic and more in this week's #AskTom. Here's what Brady had to say about Case Keenum's surprising performance, Sean Payton's gutsy calls in the Broncos' win over the Rams and how cleats can make a difference in a quarterback's throw. Case Keenum is 38, third on the depth chart and hasn't started since 2023, but he helped the Bears beat the Eagles on Monday night. What does a week like this look like for a veteran thrust into the spotlight? Brady: Well, there's definitely some nerves and anxiety as you prepare for the week. It's been a long time since you've been the starter. It's been a long time since the team really needed you to step up and play well. But, look, when you're a veteran quarterback and you've got a lot of years of experience, as that ball's kicked off and you run your first play, you settle in very quickly. There's a lot of experience you can rely on and he's really well-coached. I love this Ben Johnson offense. There were a lot of great throws out there and he made a lot of great decisions. That's what it takes. That's why you're the backup. That's why you pay ya to deliver for your team. Sean Payton went for it twice in the third quarter to tie the game in the Broncos' win over the Rams. How much of that is a coach's decision vs. the QB potentially going and fighting for the chance to win there? Brady: In the end, it's all about the head coach's decision. What I think a lot of people need to understand is that the head coach needs to be accountable for every decision — offensively, defensively or special teams. It all comes down to one guy: the head coach making the decisions. He's the one responsible in those big moments to make the call and put his team in the best position to win. Who told you to say meatball sub? Also, can I get an exact number of meatball subs that you threw during your career? Brady: Chill, chill. Relax. Everyone's got to remember, I've got three kids, OK? So, that should just point you in the right direction. And I threw a lot. I probably threw over 200 interceptions in my career. I would say somewhere between 25 and 50 [were meatball subs]. And, believe me, Coach [Bill] Belichick, he never let me forget those. Was Bill calling them meatball subs? Was that where that lingo came from? Brady: No, [Belichick would say]: "Brady, you bum." And I just took it like a man. I learned from it, and hopefully I didn't go out there and repeat them too often. Actually, I'm glad you brought that up, because I think, and what I notice so much in the NFL is there's so many people telling everybody how great they are all the time. I don't think a lot of young people understand that the best way to learn is by getting outside their comfort zone and learning from coaches who are really pushing them. Coaches are the ones who should be telling you the truth every day. I was very fortunate. I had the greatest coach in the history of the NFL. He never let me forget when I threw an interception. He never glazed over it. He didn't move on. He let me know about it, created awareness about it and he let me sit in the pain of letting the team down for a day or two before moving on. I think it was great learning for me, even though it was painful. It let me grow up. It helped me toughen up. It let me gain the respect of my teammates and coaches when they saw that, and I was able to move on and put it behind me. Did you have that perspective in the moment, or was that something that came afterwards? Brady: All of it's learned. I think the great fortune for me is, being retired for four years, I look back on all the things that allowed me to be the player I wanted to be. I'm so grateful for everybody that was on my journey and all the coaches that pushed me and pushed me every single day, when they had higher expectations for me and they knew I could achieve them and they pushed me to do that. That's what every great athlete should want. You should want a coach that's demanding and calls you out when you're not playing up to your standard, because that's going to elevate your game. Yeah, it may sting in the moment a little bit, but when you reflect back at the end of a long career, you're going to be appreciative and respectful of the coaches that did just that. How much attention did you pay to a field and the cleat choice going into a game and what did that have to do with your throwing mechanics? Brady: It was always important that you had to know the surface that you were playing on. But, listen, I loved grass fields. I hated turf fields. What we're doing to kids at turf fields in high school, college and, ultimately, when they get to the pros, the wear and tear on those bodies over time really takes a toll. I really love the grass fields. So what, it's a little bit slick? So what, it's a little bit muddy? I'd much rather fall on a grass field than not. I think the most important point when you have a field that's a little bit slick is you wear a longer seven-stud, so it digs into the surface. A lot of guys actually didn't like playing with the long seven studs. But I always felt as a quarterback, if I was able to drive the ball, I would need a really firm base in the pocket. And when I plant on the back foot of either a three-step, five-step or seven-step drop, the back cleats really allowed me to dig into the surface to transfer my ground force going backwards into going back into my hitches. If I was hitching into the throw, I could create a lot of ground force going into my target, the right amount of torque with my body — my shoulder-hip dissociation — and then, when I released the ball, I still maintained the whip. The problem is, if you lose your ground force because you're slipping on the surface, your whole mechanics shift to only using your torque and this really relaxed whip in your arm. So, I would say you become much stronger with your throw. The whole point, I would say, is to get the ground force from your legs into your torque into the whippy arm. That's how you generate the maximum force throwing a football. Equipment managers everywhere are scrambling this week after that, Tom. Brady: Hey, go figure it out, young equipment managers. articles.title: Atlanta Moves On: 3 Takeaways From Braves' Wild Card Win Over Phillies
articles.summary: The Braves pounced on the Phillies and now set a date with the Dodgers in the NLDS.
articles.body: Watch out, Dodgers. Here come the triumphant Braves.One night after the Phillies stole Game 2 of the Wild Card series with a late rally and a clutch 10th inning home run, the Braves stepped up at Truist Park in the winner-take-all finale. An unlikely hero opened a bullpen game, Michael Harris II, Ozzie Albies and Matt Olson supplied the power, and Atlanta shut the door on Philly to advance to the NLDS for a date against the two-time defending-champion Dodgers.Here are my takeaways: 1. Phillies Should Have Started Wheeler It’s a do-or-die game, and Don Mattingly’s Phillies put Aaron Nola, their unpredictable right-hander, on the hill instead of Zack Wheeler, their reliable ace. Outside of excessive concerns about Wheeler pitching on short rest, the decision to go with Nola over him made little sense well before the first pitch was thrown.Nola has been the definition of volatile for the Phillies this season, alternating between flashes of brilliant stretches and frustrating spirals. In the first half of the year, Nola produced a 5.75 ERA across 19 starts and 97 innings pitched. In the second half, he recorded a 3.33 ERA in 14 starts and 78 ⅓ innings. So the Phillies were encouraged enough by Nola’s second-half turnaround that they decided he was the better option than Wheeler, who turned in a six-inning, one-run gem against the Rays on Sunday. Going with Nola’s unpredictability was a mistake. The 33-year-old recorded the shortest postseason start of his career on Thursday against the Braves. Nola lasted just 1 ⅔ innings after coughing up a three-run home run to Michael Harris II and putting the Phillies in a 3-0 hole in the first inning.Mattingly finally turned to Wheeler at the top of the third inning, but the damage was already done. Wheeler allowed a two-run home run to Ozzie Albies in the fourth inning, but that was his only blemish. Wheeler ended up pitching four innings before his night was over, so he was clearly OK with pitching on short rest. If your best pitcher is available in an elimination game, you start him. Perhaps the Phillies were saving Wheeler for Game 1 of an NLDS that they never reached. Mattingly and the Phillies learned that lesson the hard way. 2. A Storybook Start For Ray Kerr The Braves pitching staff has been remarkable this season, serving as the primary engine behind the club’s strong season. Despite the revolving door of injuries to the rotation and bullpen, Atlanta’s pitching staff finished the season with the fifth-best ERA (3.63) in the major leagues. Most teams would collapse after losing 4–5 starting pitchers, but the Braves depth pieces and next-man-up mentality kept them elite. So it was no surprise that when the Braves called on 32-year-old southpaw Ray Kerr to take the mound in Thursday’s elimination game, he delivered. Kerr grew up in foster care, then later worked at a 7-Eleven and a movie theater in Reno, Nev., before the Mariners offered him a minor-league contract in 2017. After getting traded to the Padres for a cup of coffee, Kerr joined the Braves in 2024, and pitched in just 10 games before undergoing Tommy John surgery. He finally made it back to the mound in August this season and recorded a 1.47 ERA in nine games (one start) before he received the nod to start Thursday’s elimination game for Atlanta. In the most important outing of his career to date, Kerr held the Phillies to 3 ⅓ scoreless innings while allowing just one hit and one walk and striking out two. Even though he was just the latest pitcher to step up and deliver for these Braves, his performance was still nothing short of special given all that he had to overcome to be there in the first place. 3. Philly's Offense Faltered When It Mattered Despite the Braves’ early 3-0 lead that soon turned into a 5-0 deficit for the Phillies, the visiting club still created a handful of chances to cash in on runs. Philly just couldn’t get the job done when it mattered most, which has been an unfortunate recent October trend for the club. Their best chance to trim their deficit was in the sixth inning, when Kyle Schwarber lined a one-out single to right field and Bryce Harper followed with a double to put runners on second and third for the Phillies. But the rest of the Phillies’ lineup couldn’t hold up its end of the bargain as Alec Bohm grounded out and Bryson Stott flew out to end the inning and the threat. Again, in the eighth inning, Derek Hill led off the frame with a triple to center. Trea Turner brought Hill home on a sacrifice fly, but that was all the Phillies could muster. With two outs in the eighth, Braves manager Walt Weiss went to his best weapon — a cutthroat Chris Sale sprinting in from the bullpen to face Bryce Harper. Sale struck out Harper on four pitches, with none of those four offerings ever touching the strike zone. Sale took care of business in the ninth and punched Atlanta’s ticket to the NLDS.The Phillies went 0-for-6 with runners in scoring position and left five men on base. Their season, which was on the brink of ending without a wild-card berth after last week’s brutal collapse, finally ended in a whimper at the hands of their division-rival Braves. After multiple disappointing October endings, dating back to when the Phillies lost the Fall Classic to the Astros in 2022, it’s hard to tell where they go from here.

articles.title: Are The Browns For Real? 3 Takeaways From Browns' Dramatic Win vs. Steelers
articles.summary: The Browns are now in first place in the AFC North after their win over the Steelers. Here are three takeaways from Thursday's game.
articles.body: First-year Browns head coach Todd Monken told everyone who would listen this offseason that he thought he could win in Cleveland. And for the most part, everybody laughed. But nobody is laughing anymore. One month into the season, Monken’s Browns are now in first place in the AFC North after their wild, dramatic, 27-24 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in Cleveland on Thursday night. It took a 56-yard field goal by Andre Szmyt with 10 seconds left to do it, but the win left the Browns with a 3-1 record. Not bad for a franchise that won a total of eight games over the last two seasons. They have a young, talented team, a confident and fearless coach, and last night it sure looked like they’ve found a quarterback, too. Here are my takeaways from a night where they surely made Pittsburgh’s Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers feel old: 1. Browns Have Solved Their QB Problem … Probably When I visited Browns’ training camp this summer, Monken made it clear to me that his main issue was to "find a quarterback." He seemed to think it might even be a season-long search. But it seems pretty clear that he’s got his guy — at least for the short term. Deshaun Watson was mostly outstanding against the Steelers on Thursday night, completing 24 of 33 passes for 268 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. He was a lot better in the first half than the second, but he was also pretty good at the end of the game, when he went 4 for 5 for 46 yards. Watson has been pretty good all season too, though this was the first time he flashed some of his old potential. For the most part, he was on target, showed off his strong arm, and, maybe most importantly, he almost single-handedly kept the Steelers’ pass rush off-balance, using his mobility to get out of trouble and extend plays. Watson is 31 now and has barely played the last five years, so who knows how long this will last? But he’s coming through when it counts and the Browns are winning, so any thoughts Monken might have had about giving a shot to second-year pro Shedeur Sanders have to be on the back burner now. Back in the summer, Monken seemed ready to ride Watson as far as he could. And right now he doesn’t seem to be slowing down Maybe Sanders will still be the Browns’ quarterback of the future. It’s hard to imagine the Browns would bring Watson back next year under any circumstances once his fully guaranteed $230 million albatross of a contract finally expires. But that’s a problem for later. For now, Watson is giving Cleveland everything it needs. 2. Aaron Rodgers Still Has It … Just Not As Much As He Used To When Aaron Rodgers was leading the Steelers back from a 21-10 deficit in the fourth quarter, he looked like his younger self. He fired a strike down the field to DK Metcalf. He rolled out of the collapsing pocket and threw a 21-yard dart to tight end Darnell Washington for a touchdown. He even threw his 42-year-old body over the middle for a 2-point conversion on a quarterback sneak. It was fantastic to watch. It was just like old times. The problem is, it’s increasingly rare. Rodgers completed 22 of 40 passes for 299 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions — hardly a good game by his standards. But it’s what is beyond the numbers that really is most alarming. Until he found Metcalf deep in the fourth quarter, he struggled to throw anything beyond 15 yards. Most of his downfield throws were wobbly floaters that were way off target. And even worse, he has become a sitting duck in the pocket. Most of the time when he tries to escape, he looks like he’s running in slow motion. That’s why he took a beating from the Browns defense, which ended up sacking him five times. There are things Rodgers can still do well. He’s got a brilliant football mind and rarely makes a mistake with where he throws the ball. His release is still lightning quick. He also knows how to throw his players open, maybe better than any quarterback in the league. And, as he showed late against the Browns, he’s still clutch. He knows what to do and how to do it when the game is on the line. But his ability to be consistent is shot. His big-play skills are all but gone, only available for an occasional cameo. And that’s turned McCarthy’s attack into something of a predictable, plodding mess that feels like it moves in slow motion. That can be effective — like on their game-opening, 17-play, 78-yard, 9:48-long touchdown drive — but only in small bursts. What they need is a lot more of the Rodgers they saw in the fourth quarter, the one who can move and still fire accurate throws down the field. Unfortunately for them, it just doesn’t look like Rodgers is capable of doing that with any regularity anymore. 3. Cleveland Is Experiencing The Promise, And Problems, Of Youth This has not exactly been the NFL’s best-run franchise in the seven-year reign of general manager Andrew Berry, but he deserves some credit for this: This roster is loaded with good, young, dynamic players on both sides of the ball. If they can solve their long-term quarterback problem, they could be set up to be good for years. But all that youth seems like it’s a bit of a problem right now, because they sometimes play like they’re a bunch of inexperienced kids. The Baby Browns committed 14 penalties on Thursday night, including five (one that was declined) in the final 5.5 minutes. That included a defensive holding that gave the Steelers another shot at the game-tying touchdown, and an offside (by star edge rusher Jared Verse) on the ensuing 2-point conversion. They survived, but it’s not easy to make that many mistakes and still pull a game like this off. Better opponents are going to take advantage of that. It will be the Browns’ undoing if they somehow stay in the playoff race. Make no mistake, though: The kids are good, and they were showing off against the Steelers, particularly on offense. That includes their two terrific rookie receivers, Denzel Boston (4 receptions for 89 yards) and KC Concepcion (5 receptions for 64 yards), and two finds from last year’s draft, tight end Harold Fannin (3 receptions for 27 yards and a touchdown) and running back Quinshon Judkins (17 carries for 53 yards and a touchdown, plus six catches for 43 yards). And on defense, they’ve got a few young impact players, like edge rusher Jared Verse, whom they got in the Myles Garrett trade with the Rams, and linebacker Carson Schwesinger, the reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year. That kind of talent will carry them a long way in the future. The penalties and youthful mistakes, though, will keep holding them back.

articles.title: Asian Games: Nethra Kumanan ends long wait for maiden sailing medal with bronze
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's Nethra Kumanan finally broke her Asian Games medal jinx on Friday, clinching bronze in the women's dinghy event at the Aichi-Nagoya
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's Nethra Kumanan finally broke her Asian Games medal jinx on Friday, clinching bronze in the women's dinghy event at the Aichi-Nagoya Games to secure her first medal at the continental showpiece in her fourth appearance.The 29-year-old Chennai sailor, a two-time Olympian, finished third with 14 points overall — seven from the qualification races and seven from the final — behind Thailand's Sophia Montgomery, who won gold with five points, and Singapore's Jania Ang, who took silver with 13.In sailing, lower scores are better, with competitors awarded points corresponding to their finishing position in each race. The sailor with the lowest aggregate score wins the regatta.Nethra had entered the final day with the medal within reach and delivered when it mattered. She finished sixth in one of the two final races before winning the other to strengthen her position on the podium.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleFourth time lucky for NethraThe bronze was particularly significant for Nethra, who had endured heartbreak at previous editions of the Asian Games.She had competed at the 2014, 2018 and 2022 editions but narrowly missed out on a medal twice, finishing fourth on both occasions. Her persistence finally paid off in Aichi-Nagoya as she converted another strong campaign into a podium finish.Nethra's medal also added to India's growing sailing haul at the Games.India had already secured two sailing medals before Friday's competition. Manu Francis and Prince Noble won silver in the men's skiff event on Thursday, while Harshita Tomar and Shital Verma claimed bronze in the women's skiff competition.The women's skiff medal came after India initially finished fourth, with the position upgraded following China's disqualification.Vishnu misses out despite strong finishThere was disappointment for India's Vishnu Saravanan in the men's dinghy event as the Olympian finished fourth.Saravanan ended his final two races strongly, finishing second in both, but an accumulated qualification score of 17 left him with 21 points overall and outside the medal positions.South Korea's Jeemin Ha won gold with nine points, Hong Kong China's Nicholas Halliday took silver with 11, while Malaysia's Mohd Khairulnizam finished third with 14.Saravanan had won bronze at the previous Asian Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Not going to be easy': Ishan Kishan ahead of India-Pakistan gold medal clash
articles.summary: Ishan Kishan is not allowing the prospect of facing Pakistan in the Asian Games gold medal match to weigh on his mind, even as the India
articles.body: Ishan Kishan is not allowing the prospect of facing Pakistan in the Asian Games gold medal match to weigh on his mind, even as the India wicketkeeper-batter acknowledged the quality of the Sahibzada Farhan-led side.India booked their place in the final with a commanding 124-run victory over Sri Lanka in the second semi-final, keeping alive their hopes of defending the gold medal they won at the Hangzhou Games.Kishan was central to India's success, producing an unbeaten 80 on a difficult batting surface to help the Men in Blue post 169/7 in their 20 overs. The bowlers then completed the job in emphatic fashion, with Jasprit Bumrah, Axar Patel and Abhishek Sharma claiming two wickets apiece as Sri Lanka were bowled out for just 45 inside 10 overs.India's reward is a gold medal clash with Pakistan on Saturday, October 3.The two teams have met only once in men's cricket this year, with India winning their encounter at the Men's T20 World Cup. Pakistan, however, have a significantly different look in the Asian Games, with Farhan leading the side and the likes of Babar Azam, Shaheen Shah Afridi and Haris Rauf absent from the squad.Kishan, though, said India would not get caught up in the occasion or look too far ahead."Just keeping it simple, you don't think so much. We played today, and we know the conditions are not going to be so easy. Especially, they are also a spinner-friendly team,” Kishan told reporters in the post-match press conference.“At the same time, you know, you just don't think about what's going to happen after two days. You just keep calm, you play your shots, you be in the moment and just enjoy those crunch moments,” he added.Kishan's innings stood out even more given the conditions. While the rest of the batters struggled to find their rhythm, the left-hander remained fluent against both Sri Lanka's pace and spin attacks.The chance to win a medal has added another layer of motivation for Kishan, who is looking forward to the summit clash.“I was thinking about this, and it does make a difference in your heart, at least, you know, when you're playing for India, especially when it's about the medal. And it's not just about being related to BCCI,” said Kishan.“It's always about India here. There are so many flags going around and so many people cheering for you. So you get that feeling inside, though you don't show it. But yeah, I think you get that feeling like this is a different kind of thing, even if we have a very good side and we have those bowlers, we have those batters. But still, I feel there's a bit more pressure here, to be very honest,” he added.The India-Pakistan final will also bring renewed attention to the relationship between the two cricketing sides. Players from the two teams have not shaken hands with each other since last year's Asia Cup, and it remains to be seen whether that continues in Saturday's gold medal contest.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India added another bronze to their swelling medal tally at the Asian Games on Friday as their men’s sepaktakraw team bowed out in the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India added another bronze to their swelling medal tally at the Asian Games on Friday as their men’s sepaktakraw team bowed out in the semifinal at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Gymnasium.India went down 0-2 to hosts Japan in a tightly contested men’s quadrant semifinal, losing 12-15 and 13-15. The defeat ended their campaign with a bronze medal, but the podium finish marked another significant addition to India’s medal haul at Aichi-Nagoya.The bronze was India’s sixth medal of the day and took the overall tally to 72 — 12 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleIndia fall short against JapanIndia stayed competitive throughout the semifinal but could not convert the crucial points in either set. Japan edged the opening set 15-12 before holding their nerve to win the second 15-13 and secure a place in the gold-medal match.The result meant India finished their sepaktakraw campaign with one bronze medal.India had entered the semifinals unbeaten after topping Group A. They secured their place in the last four with a 2-1 victory over Myanmar on Thursday, winning 10-15, 15-13, 15-7.Earlier in the group stage, India had beaten Laos before defeating Vietnam 2-0 (15-12, 15-9). articles.summary: Kolkata: Gurinder Singh Sangha, a Jalandhar-based international hockey umpire and technical official who was appointed by the Asian Hockey Federation
articles.body: Kolkata: Gurinder Singh Sangha, a Jalandhar-based international hockey umpire and technical official who was appointed by the Asian Hockey Federation (AHF) as umpire manager for the hockey competition at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, has left Japan before the tournament concluded following multiple complaints of alleged sexual misconduct against him.Sources alleged that Sangha misbehaved with a female hockey official from Malaysia.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal Tally“On the pretext of mentoring and teaching her, he allegedly tried to hug her on multiple occasions and also kissed her. Following the incident, she complained to the Malaysian umpire manager,” a source familiar with the development said.Multiple sources also alleged that Sangha behaved inappropriately with a member of the hotel staff and showed her obscene videos in his room. However, TOI could not independently verify the allegation.The latest complaint is not the first allegation made against Sangha. During the Hockey India League in Ranchi in January 2025, a female umpire filed a formal complaint against him while he was serving as Umpires' Manager. Hockey India subsequently confirmed receipt of the complaint and constituted a three-member committee to conduct a preliminary investigation into the matter.According to the complaint, the female umpire alleged that Sangha's conduct during an interaction at the team hotel in Ranchi on January 20, 2025, was "unwanted and inappropriate" and left her uncomfortable. She urged Hockey India to take action and ensure a safe and respectful working environment for women officials.In a communication dated January 21, 2025, HI secretary general Bhola Nath Singh informed stakeholders that a three-member panel had been constituted in consultation with the federation's Internal Complaint Committee for Prevention of Sexual Harassment to carry out a preliminary investigation and submit its report within two days.The outcome of that inquiry could not be immediately ascertained. However, official documents show that the complaint was formally received by Hockey India and referred for investigation.The latest episode comes amid increased scrutiny of misconduct complaints within Indian hockey. Earlier this year, Hockey India removed a support staff member from a national camp after harassment allegations surfaced against him, stating that action was taken immediately after the matter came to its notice.The federation has also grappled with other complaints in recent times, including an April 2026 complaint alleging sexual harassment and abuse of authority by a Hockey India official, and a 2025 case involving a junior women's team coach.During the inaugural Women's Hockey India League, a coach was removed overnight after authorities were informed of harassment complaints involving younger players.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sujeet Kalkal ended India's wait for a wrestling gold at the Asian Games 2026 with a stunning comeback in the men's freestyle 65kg category on Friday.The 23-year-old Indian defeated Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiyev 10-9 in a dramatic final at the Nagoya City Inae Sports Center.Kalkal was trailing 2-9 for most of the bout and looked set to miss out on the gold. But he produced a remarkable late fightback, scoring eight points in a row to turn the match around and seal India's first wrestling gold at the Games.Dominant run to the finalKalkal had already beaten tough opponents from Afghanistan, Iran and Japan on his way to the final.He began his campaign against Afghanistan's Sayed Omar Zazai and fell 0-3 behind early. Kalkal then changed the match with a push-out and a shoulder throw to take a 5-3 lead.He added four more points with another throw and a roll before completing a 13-3 win by technical superiority to move into the quarterfinals.Kalkal then produced another clinical performance against Iran's Abbas Ebrahimzadehsavadkouhi. He won by technical superiority without conceding a single point.Beat Olympic championThe biggest test came in the semifinal against Japan's Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka.Kalkal trailed 0-2 after the first period but fought back in the second. He scored three points while Kiyooka managed only one, leaving the bout tied 3-3.Kalkal won the contest on criteria to book his place in the final.Eight straight points for goldKudiyev made a strong start in the final and built a 9-2 lead. The Tajik wrestler appeared to be close to winning the gold, but Kalkal refused to give up.The Indian then produced a sensational finish, scoring eight points in a row to overturn the deficit and win 10-9.The victory gave Kalkal his first Asian Games gold medal and India's first wrestling gold at the 2026 Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ankush Panghal completed a golden hat-trick for Indian boxing at the Asian Games on Friday, defeating South Korea’s Minseong Kim in the men’s
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ankush Panghal completed a golden hat-trick for Indian boxing at the Asian Games on Friday, defeating South Korea’s Minseong Kim in the men’s 80kg final to cap a memorable day for the country’s pugilists in Aichi-Nagoya.Ankush dominated the title bout, winning the opening round 4-1 before taking the second unanimously 5-0 to establish a commanding advantage. He maintained his control in the third round, winning it 4-1 to seal the gold medal with a 4-0 verdict.His triumph came after Lovlina Borgohain and Parveen Hooda had won their respective finals, making Friday a landmark occasion for Indian boxing.Lovlina defeated China’s Ziyi Bao 5-0 in the women’s 75kg final on her 29th birthday, while Parveen edged Paris Olympics bronze medallist Chen Nien-chin of Chinese Taipei 3-2 in a split decision in the women’s 65kg category.The three victories gave India a hat-trick of boxing gold medals and brought a memorable end to a day of high-stakes contests.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleAnkush dominates the finalAnkush made an emphatic start against Kim, edging the opening round 4-1 on the judges’ scorecards. The Indian then raised his game in the second, securing a unanimous 5-0 verdict to move firmly in control of the contest.With the gold within reach, Ankush stayed composed in the final round and continued to outscore his Korean opponent. He won the round 4-1 to complete a commanding performance and claim the men’s 80kg title.The victory added another gold to India’s boxing haul after the women’s finals had already delivered two major milestones.Lovlina and Parveen end 12-year waitEarlier, Lovlina produced a composed performance to defeat Bao and upgrade the silver she had won at the previous Asian Games. Her victory ended India’s 12-year wait for a women’s Asian Games boxing gold and made her only the second Indian woman after legendary MC Mary Kom to win the title.Mary Kom had claimed the women’s 51kg gold at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon.“It was a very special birthday, I'm feeling really good. I thought I'd have to gift a gold medal on my birthday. It's the first time that I got a present for myself,” Lovlina said after her victory.Parveen followed with a hard-fought win over Chen, the Paris Olympics bronze medallist, to secure her maiden Asian Games gold. Her narrow split-decision victory added another landmark moment to India’s campaign.India’s boxing contingent had already surpassed its four-medal return from the previous edition, with Priya Ghanghas, Kapil Pokhariya and Narender Berwal also securing bronze medals.The country’s best Asian Games boxing performance remains the 2010 Guangzhou edition, where Indian boxers won nine medals, including two golds. Friday’s three-title sweep provided another memorable chapter in India’s campaign at Aichi-Nagoya.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Mónica Montes, conocida en el sector como 'La Víbora del pádel', es la voz del pádel femenino en todo el mundo. articles.summary: El periodista italiano explicó en La Pizarra que el estilo de juego y su conocimiento de LaLiga encajarían con el portugués, aunque enfrió cualquier posibilidad
articles.body: Matteo Moretto volvió a pasar por La Pizarra de Radio MARCA para desgranar algunos de los movimientos que pueden marcar el mercado. Uno de los nombres propios fue el de Joao Félix, cuyo futuro volvió a quedar relacionado con el Barcelona. Moretto desveló cuál sería el deseo del futbolista: "A Joao Félix le encantaría volver al Barça, pero no tiene sitio". El periodista explicó además por qué considera que España y, especialmente, el conjunto azulgrana encajarían con las características del portugués. "Por el estilo de juego que tiene Joao Félix, por la estructura física, el nivel técnico que tiene y el conocimiento de LaLiga en España pega mucho y en el Barça aún más...", señaló. Eso sí, Moretto rebajó cualquier expectativa sobre un posible movimiento y dejó claro hasta dónde llega la información en estos momentos: "Pero quedan cosas... De momento no hay nada más que esto". Moretto también puso sobre la mesa el futuro de Owen Emeka: "Va a renovar con el Granada". El periodista explicó que el futbolista ya tuvo opciones para marcharse la pasada temporada: "La temporada pasada tuvo ofertas de clubes importantes, pero rechazó dejar el Granada y decidió renovar". Entre esos equipos apareció el Real Madrid: "Tanteó este posible fichaje, pero no se dio y Emeka decidió renovar", desveló Moretto. Aún así, el jugador continúa teniendo pretendientes: "Hay clubes que le siguen de cerca. Everton, Newcastle o Arsenal preguntaron por él". También dejó otra información sobre el director deportivo español Diego López, ahora en la Serie A: "Puede dejar el Genoa en las próximas semanas y el Burnley está interesado en él". Moretto también informó de los planes del Betis con dos de sus futbolistas: "Bartra y Bellerín están muy contentos en el Betis y el club se va a sentar con los dos para renovarles antes de enero".

articles.title: Fagioli handed Italy no.10 shirt as Mancini confirms squad numbers for France
articles.summary: The squad numbers for Italy’s upcoming Nations League test away against France have been confirmed, as Fiorentina’s Nicolo Fagioli takes over the prestigious...
articles.body:
The squad numbers for Italy's upcoming Nations League test away against France have been confirmed, as Fiorentina's Nicolo Fagioli takes over the prestigious no.10 shirt following Giacomo Raspadori's withdrawal from the squad.

Roberto Mancini faces the toughest test yet of his second spell in charge of the Italy national team, away against France at the Stade de France in what will be Zinedine Zidane's first home match in charge of Les Bleues. Kick-off is due at 19.45 BST.

Italy are coming in off the back of a 2-0 defeat at home against Belgium and a morale-boosting 4-1 win away against Turkey on Monday evening. France have beaten both Turkey and France 1-0 away from home in the September-October international break.

Francesco Pio Esposito celebrates with his brother Sebastiano Esposito during Turkiye vs. Italy in the Nations League (@azzurri)

As this is a competitive, Nations League fixture, Mancini has had to cut his list of players down to a matchday squad of 23 , leaving Massimo Pessina, Diego Coppola, Daniele Ghilardi, Eddy Koaudio, Alessandro Romano, Rolando Mandragora, Nicolo Cambiaghi and Samuele Inacio at Coverciano for this one.

Honest Ahanor was also cut from the squad ahead of the France match and has instead been made available to Silvio Baldini and the Italy U21s ahead of a crucial European Championship qualifier against Poland on Monday night.

Nicolo Zaniolo and Giacomo Raspadori have also left the squad through injury and have not been replaced.

Federico Dimarco and Bryan Cristante withdrew from the squad at the beginning of the international break and were replaced by Matteo Ruggeri and Samuele Ricci, who could both be involved against France on Friday.

BURSA, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 28: Michael Kayode of Italy celebrates scoring his team's third goal with teammate Sandro Tonali during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Türkiye and Italy at Atatürk Spor Kompleksi Matli Stadyumu on September 28, 2026 in Bursa, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images)

Pre-match reports indicate that it will be a 4-3-3 featuring Michael Kayode and Riccardo Calafiori at full-back with Alessandro Bastoni and either Giorgio Scalvini or Gianluca Mancini at centre-back.

Three out of Sandro Tonali, Nicolo Barella, Davide Frattesi and Nicolo Fagioli are expected to start, although the fact that Fagioli has been handed Italy's no.10 shirt in the absence of Raspadori might be a clue that he will be given the nod.

articles.body:
The NHL trade rumors today are the same old bits of speculation, but the news is significant. NHL commissioner Gary Bettman confronted the spate of trade requests by players weaponizing their no-trade clauses and threatened to address the matter with the NHLPA if it persists. Unfortunately, Florida Panthers center Sasha Barkov suffered an ugly injury last night and left the ice immediately. A color analyst tried to joke with Jake Hughes between periods but offended him instead, and the awkward video is amusing. Nashville is poking around defensemen on the trade block, and the Pittsburgh Penguins might look different on Saturday.

I'm kicking myself a good bit today. I was going to ask Bettman about the trade requests on Wednesday when I had the chance. I wasn't quick enough on an early Q, and then the marketing of romance novels received a few questions, and I bagged it. I think we should talk about these requests, and I think the fans' voice should be heard loudly.

I have to read up on the Steelers game today. I didn't make it to the second half before falling fast asleep. After getting out of the arena after midnight Wednesday, I caught the train out of Philly at 6 a.m. to Harrisburg, where my car was waiting—that process saves two hours of driving or taking the train the whole way—so I made the noon practice.

I think I need more cardio. Sleep is such a waste of time.

The significance is that the injury news from practice had two parts: the good and the bad. First, Blake Lizotte was absent, but Ben Kindel was back and looking pretty, pretty good at Penguins practice .

articles.title: Chicago Blackhawks lose 2nd straight game — and have been outscored 11-2 to start the season
articles.summary: SALT LAKE CITY — That was ugly. The Chicago Blackhawks were coming off a less-than-ideal season opener to Vegas, where the Stanley Cup runner-ups cruised to...
articles.body:
The Chicago Blackhawks were coming off a less-than-ideal season opener to Vegas, where the Stanley Cup runner-ups cruised to a 5-2 win . The road team struggled to do much, especially to stop the Golden Knights.

Salt Lake City was a perfect place for a rebound. The Hawks have had the Mammoth's number , winning four straight games in the NHL's newest team's brief history.

Thursday's game was a whole different story.

The Hawks (0-2-0) were overwhelmed by Utah, which emphatically defeated its Central Division opponent 6-0. The Hawks have been outscored 11-2 to start the season.

"I don't think we played very good individually, I thought we made our decisions too slow," coach Jeff Blashill said. "I didn't think we played to the level that we're capable of."

The first period, much like in Vegas, was bad for the Hawks. It was scoreless until Utah forwards Dylan Guenther and Michael Carcone scored 40 seconds apart.

Offense has been hard to come by for Blashill's team, so those early holes are steeper compared to others.

"Momentum in games matter — a lot of times when you're on the road, especially against what I think are really good teams, you're gonna get pinned in a little bit," Blashill said. "You've got to manage that and try to get out of there without giving up goals, without taking penalties, which we didn't do on either night."

Blashill's line experiments took to the ice Thursday, with line shuffles of Frank Nazar with Patrick Kane, Anton Frondell, Roman Kantserov , Teuvo Teräväinen and Tyler Bertuzzi .

"It's always fun to play with (Kane) and Roman, I thought we had some good looks there towards the end." Nazar said. "It's good going out there with everybody and trying to do our best to create something."

It might not be the best idea to mix lines this frequently with a young team, and Blashill's switches seem to be made in panic rather than strategy. The young, new-look Hawks team needs to develop chemistry with the recent roster additions.

Blashill brushed off the notion of his lineups thwarting team flow on Wednesday.

"It is what it is," Blashill said. "We're trying to find the right combos and we'll see when we get there."

The right combos were not there in the Delta Center. A below-average first period was followed by a second where Utah had 29 shot attempts with 13 on goal, compared to 12 attempts and two shots on goal for the Hawks.

Ryan Donato, Nick Lardis, Ryan Greene, Kantserov, Kane and Nazar finished with zero shots on goal. Blashill noticed that, at least.

"We've got to get to some lines that we feel can produce offense and generate chances," he said.

Lines have been ever-changing, but the defensive pairs may need a refurbishing. The Hawks blueliners combined for nine giveaways, five shots attempts blocked and a non-positive plus/minus rating for all.

"It's tough to say one or a few specific things (that went wrong) at this point," defenseman Ian Cole said. "Obviously it wasn't good enough. We're going to have to take the next 48 hours and look at it and fix some things."

Bowen Byram 's first couple of games haven't been great on his new team. Blashill did switch Byram to a pair with Levshunov for a little bit, but he doesn't have plans to involve Kevin Korchinski or Ethan Del Mastro yet.

"I'm not there, probably, we'll see," Blashill said. "We consider everything, so we'll look at it and see if we think the two other options are better than the options that played."

Cole — the 37-year-old veteran who signed a one-year, $4 million contract with the Hawks in the offseason after two seasons in Utah — received a brief but warm welcome back in the first period. Unsurprisingly, that wasn't the focus postgame.

"It was nice (but) unfortunately the outcome of the game kinda overshadows everything," Cole said. "We're professional athletes and we get judged based on whether we win or lose hockey games. Tonight was obviously not a great game."

Utah made clearing the puck near impossible, creating an endless slew of scoring chances. The Hawks spent nearly the entire game in their own zone.

The Mammoth had 65 total shot attempts, 32 on goal with five different players scoring. They also won 39 of the 54 faceoffs.

"Certainly large parts of the first and the first half of the second, we couldn't get out of our end," Blashill said. "I thought we overcomplicated it a bit again, it's just a process."

Kantserov was close to his first NHL goal in the third period, but was unable to rebound Levshunov's shot. Mammoth goaltender Karel Vejmelka (15 saves) pounced on the loose puck, just one of the highlights of his ninth career shutout.

The opening two contests couldn't have gone much worse for the Hawks, and a hungry Sabres team awaits them in Buffalo on Saturday.

"I don't think we can let it snowball; there's gonna be ups and downs through the course of the season," Cole said. "We would have preferred not to start down, but I think that there is a reality where if we can steel ourselves and we can get our mind right in how we approach the long run over the course of 84 games, we could look back at this and say, 'Hey, this could've been good for us.'"

Blashill's confidence in his team hasn't wavered so far. But he noted that Buffalo is a grand opportunity.

"You gotta go change that with your play," Blashill said. "You gotta find a way to win a hockey game Saturday against a really tough opponent in their building.

"I don't think there's any lack of belief in our group. We're 0-2, that's the fact of it. We haven't played nearly our best, but it's neither more nor less than that."

articles.title: Fantasy Football Top 5 Underrated NFL DFS GPP Plays for Week 4: Roster Michael Wilson Against the Giants
articles.summary: Michael Wilson and these four players round out the top five underrated fantasy football NFL DFS GPP plays in Week 4.
articles.body:
If you're looking to take down an NFL DFS tournament, you'll likely need to mix in players who aren't heavily rostered to differentiate your lineups from the field. Entering Week 4, fantasy football managers have a 12-game NFL DFS main slate to decipher.

Based on players' salaries and matchups on FanDuel and DraftKings, here are the top five underrated NFL DFS GPP (guaranteed prize pool) plays for Week 4.

All stats used in this article are from PFF or Sumer Sports unless stated otherwise. Offensive and defensive EPA and success rate metrics are courtesy of rbsdm.com .

C.J. Stroud, QB, Houston Texans ($7,000 FD/$5,700 DK) vs. DAL

Sunday's matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and Houston Texans is expected to be one of the highest-scoring environments in Week 4. With the Texans lacking an effective rushing attack, they are 13th in neutral pass rate (54.9%), and C.J. Stroud benefits from facing a shaky Cowboys pass defense.

Across the first three weeks, Dallas' defense is 31st in dropback EPA (0.41) and 32nd in dropback success rate (58.9%) allowed.

Jacoby Brissett, QB, Arizona Cardinals ($6,800 FD/$5,000 DK) at NYG

Jacoby Brissett produced a season-high 25.6 points on FanDuel and DraftKings in Week 3 against the San Francisco 49ers, and he'll take on the New York Giants in Week 4. New York's defense is 27th in dropback EPA (0.24) and 22nd in dropback success rate (49.6%) allowed.

Of the 24 QBs with 100-plus plays to start the season, Brissett is 11th in adjusted EPA/play (0.14), 9th in success rate (49.3%), and 9th in completion percentage over expected (CPOE; +3.8%).

Michael Wilson, WR, Arizona Cardinals ($6,200 FD/$5,500 DK) at NYG

Stacking Michael Wilson with Brissett is certainly viable in Week 4 after Wilson brought in 11 of his 17 (!!!) targets en route to scoring a season-high 20.4 points on FanDuel and 25.9 points on DraftKings in Week 3. Although Wilson's 1.36 yards per route run isn't ideal, he has the second-highest target share (27.2%) on the Arizona Cardinals, only behind Trey McBride.

The Giants have surrendered the 14th-most fantasy points per game to WRs (29.1) in the first three weeks of the new campaign.

Mack Hollins, WR, New England Patriots ($5,700 FD/$4,000 DK) at BUF

Mack Hollins could potentially be a salary-saving wideout in Week 4, as the New England Patriots are expected to play from behind and the Buffalo Bills' defense has been susceptible to the pass. While the Patriots' aerial attack has been woeful so far, Hollins paces the team in target share (19.5%), and he's posting the 19th-most yards per route run (2.17) among WRs with 15-plus targets.

In addition to giving up the 6th-most fantasy points per game to WRs (32.1), the Bills' defense is 24th in dropback EPA (0.17) and dropback success rate (50.0%) allowed.

Kenyon Sadiq, TE, New York Jets ($5,300 FD/$4,000 DK) at CHI

Rookie Kenyon Sadiq exploded for a season-high 23 FanDuel points and 26.5 DraftKings points in Week 3 against the Detroit Lions. Of the 29 TEs with 10-plus targets, Sadiq has the sixth-most yards per reception (11.9), fourth-highest route rate (90.8%), and fifth-most yards per route run (2.42).

With Adonai Mitchell potentially sidelined for a second straight week, Sadiq could be busy again in Week 4 for the New York Jets

articles.title: Juventus-Cremonese 0-1 | Friendly match report from the JTC
articles.summary: Juventus' friendly against Cremonese at the Juventus Training Center ended in a 1-0 defeat, with Bonazzoli's 12th-minute goal proving decisive. The Bianconer...
articles.body:
Juventus' friendly against Cremonese at the Juventus Training Center ended in a 1-0 defeat, with Bonazzoli's 12th-minute goal proving decisive. The Bianconeri increased the pressure in the second half and went close to an equaliser on several occasions late on, also hitting the post through Durmisi.

Juventus looked to take control of possession from the opening minutes, with Cambiaso operating in a central position in front of the defence. The first promising move came in the seventh minute when Kolo Muani found Kelly on the left. His ball into the box was intercepted by Pezzella, who got there ahead of everyone and conceded a corner.

Cremonese, however, took the lead in the 12th minute. Pezzella won the ball back on the edge of his own penalty area and launched the visitors' counter-attack. Elia found Licina, who played Bonazzoli through, and the forward made no mistake in front of Pinsoglio to make it 1-0.

A minute later, Pinsoglio was called into action twice in quick succession, producing two excellent saves to deny first Elia and then Barbieri and prevent Cremonese from immediately doubling their advantage.

Juve looked to push higher up the pitch and created their best opportunity of the first half in the 27th minute. Amaradio received the ball and fired a right-footed effort across goal, beating Agazzi but sending his diagonal strike narrowly wide.

In the 34th minute, Kolo Muani was picked out by Cambiaso and took on Luperto before going to ground following contact with the Cremonese defender, but the referee waved play on. Cremonese remained compact in the closing stages of the half, limiting the Bianconeri's space and going into the break with a one-goal advantage.

Spalletti rotated his options extensively during the second half, giving several Juventus Next Gen players minutes on the pitch. The Bianconeri looked to increase the tempo and pressure, while Cremonese sought to manage their advantage through prolonged spells of possession.

In the 59th minute, Kolo Muani went to ground again inside the Cremonese penalty area following another challenge, but once more the referee allowed play to continue. Shortly afterwards, Makiobo picked out the Frenchman with an excellent long pass. Kolo Muani crossed towards Amaradio, but the Cremonese defence recovered with a perfectly timed intervention.

As the minutes passed, Juve began to spend more time in the opposition half. In the 72nd minute, Herzuah burst forward and got a shot away without finding the target, while four minutes later Radu comfortably dealt with Vandeputte's deflected right-footed effort.

Juventus continued to search for an equaliser and, in the 79th minute, Marchisio looked for Guerra from a free-kick, only for Fulignati to race off his line and get there first.

The Bianconeri's best opportunities came in the closing stages. In the 86th minute, Corigliano put the finishing touch to a fine Juventus move before Durmisi's deflected cross-shot struck the outside of the post to Fulignati's left.

Three minutes later, Juve went desperately close to making it 1-1. Ripani collected the ball on the edge of the penalty area and unleashed a powerful left-footed strike that flew narrowly wide.

The Bianconeri kept pushing in stoppage time. In the 91st minute, Montero switched play to the left, with Herzuah forced to turn the ball behind for a corner. A minute later, Guerra won a dangerous free-kick, with Barros shown the first yellow card of the match for the foul. Marchisio stepped up in the 93rd minute and went directly for goal with his right foot, but Fulignati dived across to keep out the effort heading towards the far post.

It proved to be the final opportunity of the match. At the final whistle, Cremonese secured a 1-0 victory at the Juventus Training Center, with Bonazzoli's 12th-minute goal from Licina's assist deciding the contest.

articles.title: Lions vs. Panthers preview: 3 key matchups
articles.summary: Our Detroit Lions vs. Carolina Panthers preview identifies three key matchups.
articles.body:
It's "Sunday Night Football" and the Detroit Lions have an opportunity to string together back-to-back wins when go on the road to take on the Carolina Panthers.

Readers here at Pride of Detroit are spoiled. Truly.

Before even getting to this key matchups article, coverage throughout the week have previewed this upcoming game from many different perspectives. From Meko Scott and Morgan Cannon's "Before the Roar" podcast, Erik Schlitt's scheme breakdown , Ryan Matthews' 5 Q's , and much more from the rest of the staff and even beyond with Pride of Detroit Direct .

All of that to say, as I begin finding my own space here I hope to provide thoughts and insights with these weekly key matchup previews that meet that standard set and go beyond the surface level. Digging deeper into not only what the matchups mean for each individual player, but for the team as a whole. Not only what the matchups may dictate for each particular game, but with future in mind as well.

Every week I could write about which team is going to run the ball well and which is going to stop the run. I could write about the one-on-one wide receiver and cornerback matchup du jour every week. Rinse and repeat.

I'd rather not. And I'd bet you'd rather something more than that as well.

Ennis Rakestraw Jr. vs. Ennis Rakestraw Jr.

Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. showed flashes in his first action on the season against the Jets. His performance is by far the most meaningful development of any individual player through three games.

If you're reading this, I do not need to give you the numbers to prove the struggle of the Lions cornerbacks not only this season, but throughout the entirety of Dan Campbell's tenure. I do not need to remind you about the multiple starters that necessitated a release due to off-field incidents. I do not need to remind you about the potential trade acquisition of Joey Porter Jr. that Brad Holmes did not make.

What I may need to remind you about is that while Rakestraw is in this third year, he is just 24 years old. He was highly-touted, and often mocked to the Lions as a first-round pick in 2024 pre-draft coverage. He finished as the 32nd-best player on Daniel Jeremiah's final big board.

"About Ennis Rakestraw, has never been about his kind of what he could do and his skill set and what we were seeing on the field," explained Kelvin Sheppard. "It had nothing to do with any of that. It was always about his availability with Ennis."

I could make this a matchup between Rakestraw and wide receivers Tetairoa McMillan or Jalen Coker, but I do not believe either player is Rakestraw's biggest obstacle for successful in primetime.

"I learned that I can play in this league," Rakestraw said after his 2026 debut last week . "I finally got to play in a game, and I knew what kind of challenge it was going to be backside with No. 5, he's paid a lot of money. Just had to step up to it."

If Rakestraw can continue his upward trajectory into Sunday night and begin to establish himself as a starting cornerback, the perception of and outlook for the defense will shift dramatically. But it's up to him.

"Just like I told [Ennis] Tuesday when he was in here. I said, 'How much you play is up to you,'" Sheppard said. "We saw a very small sample size. Now lets see what that looks like on a larger scale and we'll just take it from there."

The next key matchup of the contest I wanted to specifically highlight the pass rush as it relates to quarterback Bryce Young, not the Panther's offensive line. There are a few reasons for this.

First, the Panther's offensive line is banged up with starting tackle Ikem Ekwonu on reserve/PUP, guard Damien Lewis not practicing with an elbow, and rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling limited in practice in concussion protocol. With that being the case, I fully expect the Lions pass rush to have an advantage against the offensive line. At the bare minimum, Aidan Hutchinson and Alim McNeill should be to win their individual matchups relatively consistently.

Per NFL Pro, Bryce Young currently faces the second-highest pressure rate among qualifying quarterbacks at 43.5% with the fifth-quickest average time to pressure of 2.56 seconds. On the other side of the equation, the Lions' defensive pass rush is in the top-10 in pressure rate at 39% with the second-quickest average time to pressure of 2.46 seconds. The question is not whether the pass rush will create pressure quickly, but whether Young handles the pressure well and whether his ability to extend plays will result in explosive results.

While under pressure, Young's completion percentage sits at 49%, boosted by a 5.01% completion percentage over expected. Interestingly, under pressure his air yards per attempt is 14.3 while just 7.8 when not pressured.

This feels like a make-or-break opportunity for the Lions, who are in the top five in explosive passing plays allowed this season. But with this tenancy evidenced in the metrics, there is an opportunity for Sheppard and Lions defenders to be cognizant of and to appropriately scheme against Young's disparate pattern of throwing the ball further down field when feeling the heat.

If you ran to the Panthers roster see if Ejiro Evero was one of the backup cornerbacks being thrust into a starting role due to the injuries of both starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson put them on IR , you probably aren't alone. Ejiro Evero is one of the better defensive coordinators in the NFL, leading the Panthers defense since the 2023 season. The key matchup here is about how Evero decides to scheme against the Lions' most feared offensive weapon. Not Jahmyr Gibbs. Not Amon-Ra St. Brown.

Over the first three weeks of the season, the box score would tell you that Jameson Williams has been relatively absent from the Lions offense compared to expectations. But a deeper analysis shows just how much Williams has an effective on the game and how he implants fear deep within the soul of opposing defensive coordinators.

"I was talking to [Jared Goff] about Wednesday out on the practice field," said Sheppard. "Because Saint and Jamo were like, 'why are all of these defenses going to these 2-high? Scary. They're scary.' I said, 'Yeah, I'd be scared of ya'll two as well.' But the big thing its a consensus around the league if you look at it, most touchdown drives, there is an explosive pass play on the drive. It's a real thing, guys."

The Panther's run a significant amount of zone coverage defensively (85.2%), with the vast majority of that being cover-3 zone at 48.7%.

The question is going to be how the Panthers intend to handle Williams' speed as he stretches the deep center of the field vertically, stressing free safety Nick Scott. Expect offensive coordinator Drew Petzing to test this matchup early to get as much information as possible as to the Panthers defense.

Critically, defenses have remained committed to their deep shell-coverage against Williams. But eventually the dam will break. Enough Gibbs and St. Brown gut punches play-by-play and drive-over-drive while still resulting in a consistently cool 31 points of offensive production will force someone to flip the switch. When that game comes, watch out.

Three key matchups. Three opportunities.

articles.title: Super League Grand Final: Wakefield Trinity bid to grab another Oscar-worthy moment with 'Hollywood ending' vs Warrington Wolves
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity's story of relegation to the Championship for the 2024 season to the Grand Final in 2026 is one made for Hollywood; watch Warrington Wolves take on Wakefield Trinity in the Super League Grand Final on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports from 5pm
articles.body:
Rewind to 1963 and Richard Harris rolled into town to play the role of Frank Machin in 'This Sporting Life' - the adaptation of David Storey's novel centred on a coal miner turned rugby league star.

Harris later became known for playing Dumbledore in the first two Harry Potter movies as well as roles in films including The Field, A Man Called Horse, Cromwell, Unforgiven, and Gladiator. But it was his portrayal of a gritty rugby league man that originally earned him critical acclaim.

Harris turned up to Wakefield's then-named Belle Vue Stadium for two weeks of filming with some of the 1960s stars of rugby league. Under head coach Ken Traill, Wakefield won the Championship twice, plus the Challenge Cup and Yorkshire Cup three times so Harris knew he was turning up to train with the best of the best.

Amongst the likes of Derek Turner, Neil Fox, Brian Briggs and Jack Wilkinson, Harris was to portray this rough diamond that a coach saw something in to become their star loose forward.

Of course, at moments, the film was met with the steely indignation that would have been expected. The coach and physio were furious that, due to being featured in the film, they had to pay and sign up to the Actor's Guild.

Harris tried at one point to take on Turner in a scrum to bring a realism to the film and was knocked out, cutting filming short for that day.

Despite that, Wakefield's stars could see what the film was all about.

The rugby league angle centres on the fact the spirit, clear potential, and ferocity Harris' character Machin shows in his trial game in the side is enough to convince the coach he is worth a shot, that this player can be moulded from raw ability to fulfilled talent.

It is something not too dissimilar to what is on display with many of the current star players in Wakefield's Grand Final side. Caleb Hamlin-Uele was close to giving up on his rugby league dream and was working in a factory when he got the call to come and join Wakefield in the Championship. He is now close to an international call-up for England.

A similar story can be told of Caius Faatili, the pair of props becoming somewhat of an unstoppable duo when they come on for their side and wreak havoc. They have journeyed from the coal mine to stardom. They have embodied the character of Machin.

The club as a whole too, has been on a journey that scriptwriters would be able to mould into a drama. The twists and turns, the ups and down. From relegation in 2023 to these heights in 2026. From fighting to keep the lights on to thriving.

Then add in Jack Sinfield playing in his first Grand Final while his dad delivers the match ball after finishing his latest gruelling challenge for the MND Community.

To put it simply, those who love Wakefield, adore Wakefield, worship Wakefield would admit that they do not feel like they should already be at this point. Speaking to fans just days out from their biggest day in over half a century, they cannot hold in their sheer disbelief that the moment has arrived so soon.

Of course, the backing from owner Matt Ellis has sped up their trajectory and the Wakefield of today is a far cry from the Wakefield of even 10 years ago.

That being said, even those who thought it may come one day did not think it would be this day.

Harris was Oscar-nominated in the Best Actor category for his role in the film at the 36th staging of the Academy Awards. The award eventually went to Sidney Poitier for his portrayal of Homer Smith in Lilies of the Field.

However, if Wakefield go on to achieve the Super League fairytale that could be on the horizon, who is to say that they are not on the precipice of their second Oscar nomination.

Frank Machin: We don't have stars in this game, Mrs Weaver, that is soccer.

How to watch the Super League Grand Final

The Super League Grand Final takes place at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports+ .

The match will take place at 6pm, with coverage on Sky Sports from 5pm.
