articles.title: ‘Sometimes in chess there are just these blind spots’: Nihal Sarin looks back at his Chess Olympiad loss to Uzbekistan | Exclusive
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: World champion Dommaraju Gukesh was patiently following the game between his compatriot Nihal Sarin and Uzbekistan's Nodirbek Yakubboev in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: World champion Dommaraju Gukesh was patiently following the game between his compatriot Nihal Sarin and Uzbekistan's Nodirbek Yakubboev in Round 6 of the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand.The other three boards had already ended in draws, Gukesh's own game against Shamsiddin Vokhidov among them, which meant the entire match, and India's chance to overtake the hosts at the top of the standings, rested on Nihal's result.For a while, it looked like it would go India's way. After 35 moves, Nihal had built a genuinely promising position.Then came the sequence that undid it, a blunder that handed away his queen. Gukesh, who had been a silent observer all this while, looked like he couldn't believe what he'd just seen. As he turned to walk away, he buried his face in his palm in disbelief, before turning back to the board for one last look. He ran his hand over his face once again and walked away, visibly distraught.India lost the match to the team that would go on to win the tournament outright.More than a week on, the Indian chess circle is still replaying what might have happened had that one moment gone differently. Nihal, who is now back in India, took TimesofIndia.com through the entire experience of Samarkand.The moment itselfNihal made a strong start to the campaign with three consecutive wins and then two draws in the early rounds, before the Uzbekistan match changed the shape of things."Against Uzbekistan, it was really unfortunate," he, who was playing black that day, recalled. "Against Indonesia, I was actually completely losing at some point — there are a lot of what-ifs in these events, but it is what it is. Unfortunately, things didn't go my way against Uzbekistan. I was playing a really good game, but I made a very unfortunate miss. It proved too costly."Against Indonesia, Nihal was India’s sole winner, salvaging the match and ensuring the team did not drop points.Beyond the result itself against Uzbekistan, what has stayed with Nihal is the fact that he had no idea what he had missed at the time."No, actually not at all," he said, when asked if he'd spotted the mistake against Yakubboev immediately. "That was the weird thing. Generally, when you miss something like this, at least after making the move, you spot it. But I was completely oblivious to it until he made the move, which is quite uncharacteristic."Realisation only arrived with Yakubboev's reply."When he played 38.Ne6, only then did I realise what I had done wrong. Funnily enough, it's a fairly simple tactic; a bit unusual, maybe, but fairly simple regardless," he added.Gukesh and Srinath also missed itAnd Nihal was not the only one from his team to miss the sequence, as the Kerala-born grandmaster revealed, "The funny thing was that Gukesh was watching the game. He was in the hall. Apparently, he had also missed it completely. Our captain, Srinath (Narayanan), had missed it as well."It was a bit strange, because of course I should see it; we should all see it, in general. But sometimes there are just blind spots. It's a bit weird. It's a fairly simple tactic, but all three of us completely missed it. I don't know. It was strange."Even the commentary booth, armed with engines, nearly let it slip by. Vidit Gujrathi, present on the ChessBase India commentary panel for a brief moment that day, hadn't noticed the entire sequence either."Vidit was telling me that he was in the commentary room and also saw it only when the engine pointed it out in one variation," Nihal revealed. "Not many people saw it coming, which is a bit strange considering it's not the hardest tactic. Sometimes in chess there are just these blind spots. It's very hard to explain, but it happens."It stayed a talking point inside the camp afterwards too."It's just a weird thing. Sometimes you miss things a bit inexplicably. We are all quite strong grandmasters, and almost all of us missed something. It's very hard to explain," the 22-year-old grandmaster added.Picking himself back upThe team's loss that day made the aftermath heavier than a single bad result might otherwise have been."It was, of course, really tough, especially because the team also lost a very crucial match. But it was very important to have the support of the team and my coach," Nihal continued. "The team was very nice. All of them were telling me to keep my head up. I had actually managed to play a very high-quality game until that point. It happens, and all of us have been in that situation."The guilt, he said, is something he had to actively resist rather than something that simply faded."It's also very hard not to feel responsible, but you have to remember that we win and lose as a team. It's not an individual thing. All of us have been in this situation, so we understand," he added.What-ifs, and refusing to entertain themAsked whether he expects to look back someday and wonder if that one result cost India gold, Nihal's answer was less about denial than about how he's chosen to frame sport generally."It's possible, of course. But there are just no what-ifs in sport. Everything is very hard to judge. It is what it is. We just have to accept it," he further noted."Against Indonesia, we could have easily lost the match. And against Germany, we were honestly completely cooked. Against Azerbaijan, we had a chance, and then we drew. These what-ifs are very easy to fantasise about, and it's logical to think that way, but ultimately I don't think everything happens by accident — the pressure is what creates these moments."Of course, winning gold would have been brilliant, but credit to Uzbekistan, they played amazing chess, all of them, at a very high level, and they completely deserved it."First Olympiad with the senior teamThis was Nihal’s first Chess Olympiad with the main team. He now has a silver medal, and countless memories to go with it. "Of course, definitely, I would love to play it (Chess Olympiad) again. It was a lot of fun. I really enjoyed the atmosphere and everything," he shared."The general vibe was very, very nice. I personally enjoyed it a lot. It's also very nice to see so many people from so many different parts of the world, which I don't think you can see in any other tournament. You see so many players from so many places, some of which we may not even have heard of. It's very interesting."Summing up the overall experience, he added, "I think the team performance was very good. We all played pretty good chess. I don't think any of us were at our best, for sure. But we still managed to play some really good games, and everyone stepped up when it mattered most."What comes next for Nihal SarinThere's little time for Nihal to dwell on the ifs and buts of the Chess Olympiad. "I'm planning to play the European Club Cup in Montenegro, which starts on October 17. After that, I don't know. But yes, there will definitely be some break, and I'm very much looking forward to it."ALSO READ: ‘If India won a medal, we owe it to her’: Captain Swayams Mishra on Savitha Shri’s Chess Olympiad heroics | ExclusiveNot much of a globetrotter, Nihal reveals what relaxation means to him, adding, "There's a tennis club near my home, and I go pretty much every day. It really helps. It's very good exercise, and I think it also helps you feel good mentally."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India's golden day: Six gold medals across boxing, archery, wrestling and hockey highlight Asian Games Day 13
articles.summary: India produced a stunning six-gold haul on the penultimate day of the Asian Games on Friday, with the women's hockey team, three boxers, archers and
articles.body: India produced a stunning six-gold haul on the penultimate day of the Asian Games on Friday, with the women's hockey team, three boxers, archers and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal leading a late surge that took the country into the top five of the medal table.India moved to fifth place with 76 medals - 16 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze. India have more medals than fourth-placed Uzbekistan, who have 65, but trail them by four gold medals.The strong showing on Friday has given India's campaign a major boost after a mixed run earlier in the Games.Hockey ends 44-year waitThe biggest moment came in women's hockey as India beat defending champions China 1-0 to win their first Asian Games gold in the sport since 1982.Lalremsiami scored the only goal of the final with a superb reverse-stick strike in the 10th minute. But the goal was only the beginning of India's challenge as China kept pushing for an equaliser.Goalkeeper Bichu Devi and the Indian defence stood firm through long periods of pressure. The players repeatedly put their bodies on the line to protect their one-goal advantage.The victory also gave India direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, one of the key targets for coach Sjoerd Marijne's side.The final started an hour late after the team buses of both finalists were caught in a traffic jam caused by an accident unrelated to either team. Once the match began, India struck early and then held on brilliantly.Three boxing goldsIndian boxing enjoyed its most successful Asian Games in terms of gold medals, with Lovlina Borgohain, Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal all finishing on top.Lovlina celebrated her 29th birthday with a 5-0 win over China's Ziyi Bao in the women's 75kg final. She improved on the silver medal she won at the previous edition.Parveen then edged Chinese Taipei's Paris Olympic bronze-medallist Chen Nien-chin 3-2 in a split decision to win the women's 65kg gold.Ankush completed the golden hat-trick with a win over his opponent in the men's 80kg final. He became the first Indian male boxer since Amit Panghal in 2018 to win Asian Games gold.The three golds took India's boxing tally to six medals. Priya Ghanghas (60kg), Kapil Pokhariya (90kg) and Narender Berwal (+90kg) also won bronze medals.India's previous best overall boxing haul at the Asian Games came at Guangzhou 2010, when the team won nine medals - two gold, three silver and four bronze.Lovlina and Parveen also joined MC Mary Kom as Indian women boxers who have won Asian Games gold.Sujeet stages stunning comebackWrestler Sujeet Kalkal produced one of the biggest comebacks of the Games to win gold in the men's 65kg category.His campaign began with a 13-3 technical superiority win over Afghanistan's Sayed Omar Zazai. He then beat Iran's Abbas Ebrahimzadehsavadkouhi by technical superiority without conceding a point.In the semifinal, Sujeet faced Japan's Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka and won 3-3 on criteria.The final against Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev looked to be slipping away when Sujeet fell 2-9 behind.But the Indian wrestler refused to give up. Using his speed and technique, he scored eight points in a row to turn the contest around.Sujeet first cut the deficit to 8-9 before producing a decisive takedown with around 20 seconds left. He then defended his lead to win 10-9 and claim the gold.Historic gold for women's recurve teamIndia's women's recurve archery team started the day's gold rush by beating 10-time Olympic champions South Korea 5-3 in the final.Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod kept their composure in difficult windy conditions to register a historic win.The result gave India their maiden Asian Games gold in the women's recurve team event.Kumkum returned to the range later in the day and teamed up with Dhiraj Bommadevara to win silver in the mixed recurve team event. They lost 3-5 to China in the final.The men's recurve team of Bommadevara, Sanjay Bhoge and Neeraj Chauhan also finished with silver after a 1-5 loss to South Korea.India have now won seven archery medals at these Games — four gold, two silver and one bronze. The compound archers had earlier completed a clean sweep of the team gold medals.More medals add to India's haulIndia also picked up medals in sailing and sepaktakraw on a highly productive day.Nethra Kumanan won bronze in the women's dinghy event, while Harshita Tomar and Shital Verma secured bronze in the women's skiff.The men's quadrant team won a bronze medal in sepaktakraw.India's six gold medals on Friday have lifted the country to fifth in the standings and provided a strong push towards the closing stages of the Asian Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Analyzing Every NHL Team's Odds of Winning the 2027 Stanley Cup
articles.summary: We are less than one week into the 2026-27 NHL season, and you know what that means: There's still time to place a bet on virtually any team you want to win the Stanley Cup.
articles.body:
We are less than one week into the 2026-27 NHL season, and you know what that means: There's still time to place a bet on virtually any team you want to win the Stanley Cup.

At the beginning of the season, the odds are as even all around as they're going to get. This means you can find value in unexpected places and get some bang for your buck if you feel strongly about any of the top dogs.

Using FanDuel's season-opening odds , let's analyze each NHL team's odds of winning the 2027 Stanley Cup.

Editor's note: Odds are constantly changing, especially game-by-game at the beginning of the season. The odds used here were as of Wednesday, Sept. 30.

Nothing to see here, folks -- even the staunchest Canucks fans of all are already looking forward to the draft.

At least they're putting on a show and putting up a fight to start the season, with a 7-goal effort in a 9-7 loss against the Oilers in Game 2.

After opening night's 6-1 loss to the Kraken, many are wondering whether Seattle looks promising or the Flames are just that bad.

The jury's still out on the Kraken, but yes, the Flames are definitely that bad. This is the time in their rebuild when they've got a stocked prospect pool stewing, but nothing close to a complete NHL team currently on the ice.

In the Pacific, anything is possible, so there honestly could be some long-shot value in betting on the Kraken to make the playoffs. Are we overreacting to a solid opening-night win? Maybe.

Still, +20000 odds to win the actual Stanley Cup is about right for Seattle right now. They're still searching for that game-breaking player.

Staff Predictions for Stanley Cup Winner 🔮

Showtime is back where he belongs in Chicago, but will he bring the glory days along with him? It's a long shot, and so are the Blackhawks' +15000 odds to win the Cup.

They're taking some positive steps, but they've still gotta find the perfect winger for Connor Bedard, and the young core still needs a season or two before entering the playoff window, let alone winning the Cup.

It's pretty tough to evaluate the Jets until they make the much-anticipated Connor Hellebuyck trade. We can tell you one thing, though: It's hard to imagine the team getting better after trading the best goaltender in the world.

The Jets could make a few savvy moves and get back in the conversation next season, but these odds feel fair.

Much like the Jets and Hellebuyck, the Red Wings are tough to evaluate before hiring a long-term GM and deciding whether to trade (or keep!). Dylan Larkin. Still, the drama, trade request, and lack of roster improvement are enough to tell us these +10000 odds to win the Cup are fair.

The Blues are expected to take a few steps forward this season, with Robert Thomas stepping into a captain role and some savvy off-season acquisitions like Mason McTavish.

They've still gotta get back in the playoffs before they even sniff a Cup. We'll see if Jordan Binnington and Co. get back in it this season and go from there, but it's definitely not time to bet on them to win the Stanley Cup.

The Predators are headed in a positive direction after years of back-and-forth and disappointment. New GM Chris MacFarland has already moved the needle with off-season shakeups like acquiring Ross Colton and Jack Drury from his former team, the Avalanche.

Regardless, the West is an unforgiving gauntlet, and the Predators have to prove to all of us that they're really back before we go calling them Cup contenders.

The Islanders are entering year two of the Matthew Schaefer era, and year one showed us he is one of the most exciting young players in the league.

We can be almost certain that the defenseman will one day bring the Islanders back to glory, and that day might come soon. For now, though, he's still a teenager, and the Islanders have to acquire a few more goal-scorers and fix their power play if they want to sniff a Stanley Cup.

Will David Pastrňák finally win that elusive Stanley Cup now that he's been named captain of the Bruins? Perhaps one day, and hey, Boston is off to a great start with a strong opening-night win that featured a goal from new acquisition JJ Peterka.

Playoffs aren't out of the question this year, but the rest of the elite competition is just too good to consider the 2026 Bruins a Cup contender.

The Rangers made a ton of moves this offseason, and it seems the oddsmakers approved as New York's Cup odds jumped to +6500.

You gotta wonder what the odds were for a home-opening goalie goal from Igor Shesterkin. What a moment.

Anyway, for as much improvement as the Rangers have shown in avoiding a season-opening scoring drought, the East is equal parts stacked and unpredictable. The odds are trending in the right direction with the team, but it's too soon to start spreadin' the news.

The Blue Jackets made out decently enough in acquiring Matthew Knies for Kirill Marchenko, but a team that is desperate for goals still lost a goal-scorer. It's tough to see them maintain the playoff-bubble status they had last year, and these +6500 Cup odds are reasonable, if a bit generous.

Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin, and Erik Karlsson are back for at least one more attempt at a Stanley Cup. While they re-entered the playoffs last season, there appears to be little gas in the tank.

Will they be able to jump-start this car and rev up the engine, knowing it's their last good opportunity, or is there genuinely nothing left? We'll have to see, and these +6500 Cup odds reflect that uncertainty.

Despite a 7-0 home-opening loss to the Penguins, the Flyers' Cup odds are significantly higher. Obviously, Philadelphia's first-round trouncing of the Penguins last season has much to do with that, but it feels like it inflated their odds this season just a bit too much.

The Flyers overperformed and shocked themselves last season. They've got some great pieces, and we're delighted with Porter Martone's trajectory this season, but they still need to find an answer at elite center.

In the Pacific, anything is possible. It's certainly possible that the Sharks not only make the playoffs for the first time in the Macklin Celebrini era, but also win the whole division.

Is the 2027 Stanley Cup in the cards, though? Probably not. Making the playoffs and getting that first taste is more than enough this season. It's still telling that we're all so optimistic about these Sharks right now that they've jumped teams that made the playoffs last season in these odds.

Leo Carlsson and Cutter Gauthier might've been expensive as heck, but hey, they were signed to this roster before camp and came into this season as focused as can be.

Will the Ducks be able to take the next step after making the playoffs and taking down the Oilers in the first round last season? While that's entirely possible, the West is top-heavy, and reaching the Cup Final will be a battle.

The Senators having better odds than the Ducks to win the Cup is pretty surprising. The Ducks are returning their entire core, while the Senators lost their most important player, Brady Tkachuk.

The oddsmakers are likely heavily weighing the top-heavy nature of the West here. They are probably also weighing the fact that the past three Cup winners have come out of the East.

I still wouldn't bet on the Senators to win the Cup.

The Kings have made the playoffs only to lose in the first round for almost a decade now. If you really think this is the year they're going to not only make it out of round one but also hoist a Cup, feel free to bet on them at +3300 odds. I certainly wouldn't.

Only Toronto could go from the No. 1 pick in the draft lottery to pretty decent odds of winning the Stanley Cup.

The Leafs had a positive offseason with tons of moves, like acquiring Sergei Bobrovsky and bringing No. 1 pick Gavin McKenna into the fold. It isn't realistic to think the team that has struggled to make it out of the first round, even at its best, is going to jump back in and win it all.

The cathartic 2025-26 season for the Sabres was special in so many ways, but now it's time to focus on perennial playoff appearances and working towards a Cup. Buffalo lost some key players this offseason, including Alex Tuch and Bowen Byram, but their young core took major steps forward and feels ready to take on bigger roles.

We're all waiting to see if the Sabres will maintain success and keep building on it, so +3000 Cup odds are pretty fair for this season.

The Mammoth have proved so far that they are willing to do what it takes to stay in the conversation, upgrade the team, and keep chipping away at the roster to make the playoffs. Logan Cooley's health will no doubt give this team an upgrade, but did the roster overperform last season on the way to the playoffs? We'll see.

Can Jack Hughes stay healthy, can the team survive the loss of Jacob Markstrom in net, and is there any chance, in H-E-double hockey sticks, that Quinn Hughes makes a mid-season signing and trade to play with his brothers?

If the answer is "yes" to two out of these three questions, the Devils could make it back into the playoffs. But we're in no place to discuss the Devils winning the Stanley Cup until this happens.

Hopes are as high as ever for the Habs, as they should be: This young roster hasn't even reached its prime, and every year it's like each piece of the team keeps raising the ceiling.

Could Nick Suzuki win the Hart this year? Could Lane Huston win the Norris? Regardless of individual trophies, the Habs will join the Cup conversation this year. Even +2200 odds feel quite modest.

Now that the Hurricanes have the Conference Finals monkey off their back, we look to the Stars and wonder if they're ever going to make it all the way despite their many unsuccessful trips to the Western Conference Finals. It just feels like such a tall task given the top-heavy talent out West, but perhaps Jason Robertson's one-year deal lights the fire that finally takes a stacked-yet-disappointing team all the way.

Brock Faber's preseason skull fracture is a gigantic and devastating blow to a team that needs every ounce of luck it can get. We'll have to see what his recovery looks like, whether the Wild can replace all the depth scoring they lost in the offseason, and whether the noise surrounding Hughes' extension becomes a distraction.

The Wild have many questions to answer in an unforgiving Central Division.

The team that refuses to leave us alone is back, and Nikita Kucherov and Andrei Vasilevskiy are sharp as ever. Between Victor Hedman's return and the acquisition of John Carlson, it's tough to see the Lightning bowing out of the playoffs this season. To be fair, it's also tough to see them going all the way to the Cup.

The Golden Knights made it to the Cup Final last season, but they had to part ways with their top scorer Pavel Dorofeyev. While they've still got a seemingly unstoppable Mitch Marner, Jack Eichel, and tons of other high-end talent, it's hard to stomach the loss of Dorofeyev and Carter Hart's historically bad Cup Final performance last season.

They've got to keep up the scoring and keep an eye on their goaltending situation if they're to make it back to the Final this year.

Not only is Alex Ovechkin back for one last go, but the Capitals also did well in updating the team in the offseason, with Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou now in the fold.

It seems likely the Capitals are going to bounce back. They missed the playoffs last season due to a crazy battle in the East, but they had more wins than the Golden Knights, who made it all the way to the Cup Final.

We all know how desperate the Oilers are to win a Cup in the last year of Connor McDavid's contract, but that doesn't mean they're automatically in the conversation.

They've had a wacky win and a wacky loss to start the season, an indication that we're in for another year of drama for this team. If everyone stays healthy and focused, there's a chance Edmonton makes it out of the West — especially with goaltender Freddie Andersen in the fold. But +1000 odds feel a bit generous considering last season's first-round exit.

The reigning champions are tied for the second-best betting odds to win the 2027 Stanley Cup. Their roster is nearly identical to last season's, save for one big change: goalie Freddie Andersen signed with the Oilers.

Will the Hurricanes get Hellebuyck? That would likely give them the outright lead in Cup odds. Right now, a three-way tie is probably fair.

Does Colorado have one more Cup win in the tank with this core? If Nathan MacKinnon's opening-night gusto, featuring two goals and a fight, has a say, we're thinking yes.

Cale Makar became the richest player in NHL history this offseason. He and MacKinnon are still in their prime and hungry; meanwhile, Colorado's got nothing left in the prospect tank.

The pressure is on, and if it wasn't happening last year, it could be now or never again for these Avalanche. They're certainly the most likely team from the West to hoist the Cup this season, and the odds reflect that.

We get it: The Panthers are back. After a devastating year full of injuries and missed playoffs, the core of this roster is healthy, intact, and ready to compete for a third Cup in four years.

It's hard to imagine they'll miss the playoffs, but are they really one of the three most likely teams to win the 2027 Stanley Cup? Bringing Brady Tkachuk into the fold is interesting from both a morale and skill standpoint, and I'm intrigued to see whether Jacob Markstrom can consistently be the goaltender he is at his best.

It's still a lot to ask of a team to go from missing the playoffs one year to raising the Cup the next.

If anyone can do it, it's these Panthers, and the top three odds are fair. It would be one thing if they were in the outright lead for the Cup betting odds, but we'll give them part of a three-way tie. We suppose an opening-night win over the reigning champs impacted this.

articles.title: Connor Bedard secured $75 million at just 21: How the Blackhawks superstar turned three NHL seasons into a massive payday and franchise-defining contract

articles.body: Connor Bedard’s ascent with the Chicago Blackhawks has reached a huge financial milestone after the 21-year-old forward signed a five-year, $75 million contract extension. The deal is worth $15 million per year and keeps the former No. 1 overall pick under contract through the 2030-31 NHL season.The deal comes after Bedard has led the Blackhawks in scoring all three seasons. His latest campaign had career highs of 30 goals, 45 assists and 75 points in 69 games, adding further weight to a contract that ranks him among the NHL’s highest-paid players by annual value.Connor Bedard’s contract structure and NHL career impactThe extension is a significant raise from Connor Bedard’s entry-level contract and shows the quick rise he’s making as the centerpiece of the Chicago Blackhawks’ rebuilding project. The first overall pick in the 2023 NHL Draft, he took on one of the franchise’s most important offensive roles.Contract detailConnor BedardTeamChicago BlackhawksContractFive years, $75 millionAverage annual value$15 millionContract period2026-27 to 2030-31Age when signed21Draft positionNo. 1 overall, 20232025-26 points75Career NHL points203Bedard scored 61 points in 68 games to win the Calder Trophy as the NHL’s top rookie in his first season. He followed that campaign with two more seasons as the leading scorer for Chicago. He has scored 203 points (75 goals, 128 assists) in his first 219 regular-season games.SeasonGamesGoalsAssistsPoints2023-24682239612024-25822344672025-2669304575Career21975128203The five-year term also gives the Chicago Blackhawks a defined window around their young franchise cornerstone. The roster was also strengthened by veteran additions such as Jordan Greenway and Ian Cole, who came to play around the young core.But Bedard’s return has been slowed by an injury to his left shoulder. articles.title: Trail Blazers fire new TV announcer after racist posts resurface hours after he was hired
articles.summary: The Portland Trail Blazers fired new play-by-play television broadcaster Braiden Bell on Thursday when past inappropriate social media posts resurfaced just hours after the team announced his hiring.
articles.body: The Portland Trail Blazers fired new play-by-play television broadcaster Braiden Bell on Thursday when past inappropriate social media posts resurfaced just hours after the team announced his hiring. “The Portland Trail Blazers have zero tolerance for racist, sexist, or harmful comments,” the team said in a statement Thursday night. “Social media posts made by our recently announced play-by-play broadcaster are in clear violation of team and league policies, as well as our values and expectations. Therefore, we will not be moving forward with this broadcaster.” Bell had been the play-by-play announcer for the WNBA’s Phoenix Mercury and the G League’s Valley Suns before the Trail Blazers announced they had hired him on Thursday to replace longtime broadcaster Kevin Calabro. Hours later, posts surfaced that were apparently made on X by an account with Bell’s name from 2012 and 2013. The posts were first reported by KGW-TV in Portland, which said they were made when the 29-year-old Bell was a teenager. “We did not meet our own bar in this process, and for that we apologize to Blazers fans and to Rip City,” the team’s statement said. “We believe strongly that everyone who is a part of Rip City should feel welcome and safe and we will make sure that our new broadcaster reflects these values. We will do better.”

articles.title: Arrows that rewrote history: How Ankita, Kirti and Kumkum gave their fathers’ faith a golden finish at Asian Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A father sold cardboard sweet boxes in a tiny shop in Amravati. Another awoke at 4 am to deliver milk door to door in Kolkata.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A father sold cardboard sweet boxes in a tiny shop in Amravati. Another awoke at 4 am to deliver milk door to door in Kolkata. The third worked his small farmland in Jind. All three parents backed their daughters’ sporting dreams, defying doubt and social pressures.On Friday, at the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Multipurpose Square, the daughters repaid that faith with a gift beyond price. The seasoned Ankita Bhakat, the unheralded Kirti Sharma and 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod did what India had never done — beat 10-time Olympic champions South Korea 5-3 for the country’s first-ever Asian Games gold in women’s recurve team archery.The significance was immense. Korea had won every women’s team recurve title since 1998 and arrived with Tokyo Olympic champion Kang Chae-young, alongside Oh Ye-jin and Lee Yunji. India, which had never even reached the Asian Games final in this event, first beat China 5-1 in the semifinals.The final needed nerves of steel. Both sides drew the opening two sets, 54-54 and 56-56, before Korea faltered with three successive 8s in the third. India shot 55 to move 4-2 ahead. Korea answered with 54 in the fourth but Kirti’s opening 8 was upgraded to 9 on review, lifting India to 54 and sealing the draw — and the gold.“We can't describe our feelings in words. This medal is not only for us but for our parents, their sacrifices and our country too,” Kirti said. Ankita, who had endured years of hardship before becoming a veteran of the recurve circuit, said the team had trained for such pressure”. Kumkum summed up her astonishing composure, saying, “I always visualised this, and now it’s happened. It’s part of the process.”Behind the triumph were very different struggles. Kumkum began in 2018 with a bamboo bow; her grandmother financed a Rs 3,000 wooden upgrade, while her father later got her a second-hand recurve bow that she has used for years.Kirti’s farming family borrowed a Rs 60,000 loan for her first recurve bow, even as relatives questioned spending on a daughter’s sporting career. Initially considered too thin to handle a professional bow, she later topped the national trials.Ankita spent six years shooting wooden and bamboo bows before obtaining proper recurve equipment, with left-handed gear particularly difficult to find. She later began using prize money won during competitions to support her father’s modest income and family.The day produced more archery silver medals for India. Kumkum later combined with Dhiraj Bommadevara, but the duo lost 3-5 to China in the mixed recurve final after beating Japan 5-3 in the semifinals. Dhiraj, Yashdeep Bhoge and Neeraj Chauhan then lost the men’s recurve final 1-5 to Korea, after beating Iran 6-0 in the last four to settle for runners-up finish.For Kumkum, the competition is not over: she next turns to the individual event on Saturday. For India, however, the golden arrow has already landed — in history.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WWE, AEW Rumors on Drew McIntyre, Sheamus and 'Rare' Gimmick Match for Bayley vs. Lyra Valkyria
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from WWE and AEW.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from WWE and AEW.

McIntyre Reportedly Expected Back in WWE Soon

WWE x AAA Worlds Collide Highlights & Reaction 💥

Drew McIntyre's lengthy absence from WWE programming reportedly may be coming to an end in the near future.

According to Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter (h/t WrestlePurists ), McIntyre is expected back on WWE TV "soon" since he has finished up most of his acting commitments, including a WWE "micro drama" also starring Jacob Fatu and Joe Hendry.

PWInsider.com (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News) added that McIntyre recently attended meetings and filmed promotional material for the micro drama at WWE headquarters.

McIntyre, 41, last appeared on WWE programming at WrestleMania 42 in April when he lost an unsanctioned street fight against Fatu.

Leading up to WrestleMania, McIntyre had been embroiled in a months-long rivalry with Fatu, and it ultimately cost him the WWE Championship, as Fatu interfered in Drew's title defense against Cody Rhodes in March.

McIntyre had surprisingly beaten Rhodes for the WWE title in January in a Three Stages of Hell match, making him a four-time world champ.

While not always presented on the same level as the company's unquestioned top stars in Rhodes and Roman Reigns, McIntyre has long been a key figure in WWE and a perennial world title contender.

He has been a major missing piece from WWE programming over the past six months, and he will undoubtedly provide the roster with a significant boost whenever he does return.

AEW's Reported Stance on Signing Sheamus

Longtime WWE Superstar Sheamus is reportedly on the radar of some people in AEW following his surprising WWE departure.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), AEW has interest in signing Sheamus and is expected to do so.

There are reportedly members of the AEW roster who would like to see AEW bring in the 48-year-old Irishman as well.

Fightful Select (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats) reported in July that Sheamus would be leaving WWE upon the expiration of his contract after he rejected WWE's attempt to restructure his deal.

It was later reported by Fightful Select (h/t Fightful's Ishaan Sharma ) that Sheamus would officially become a free agent on Oct. 1.

Now that the date has come and gone, Sheamus is free to sign anywhere he pleases, and AEW stands out as the most obvious landing spot.

AEW has not shied away from shining accomplished WWE veterans with Kofi and Austin Creed of The New Level being the most recent example.

Sheamus put together a Hall of Fame resume during his nearly 20-year run in WWE.

The Celtic Warrior was a four-time world champion, three-time United States champion and five-time tag team champion, in addition to winning the Royal Rumble, Money in the Bank and King of the Ring one time each.

Sheamus's physical in-ring style would seemingly fit well in AEW, so it won't be a shock if that is ultimately where he ends up.

Bayley, Valkyria Reportedly Lined Up for Unique Gimmick Match

WWE is reportedly planning something out of the ordinary for an upcoming match between Bayley and Lyra Valkyria.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Mukherjee ), the eventual blowoff match in the Bayley vs. Valkyria rivalry may include a stipulation that is considered "rare" for the women's division.

No additional specifics were given, and it is unclear if the creative team has 100 percent decided to move forward with that particular idea.

One stipulation that the match reportedly won't include, however, is Hell in a Cell, which is a match that has included women on only four occasions.

Bayley competed in each of the past two women's Hell in a Cell matches, losing to Sasha Banks in 2020 and Bianca Belair in 2021.

Some stipulations that aren't particularly common for WWE women's matches and could potentially be in play include an I Quit match, a Last Woman Standing match or a strap match.

The feud between Bayley and Lyra began in June when Valkyria turned on her tag team partner and friend.

After that, Valkyria beat Bayley at Saturday Night's Main Event and then beat her again on the Sept. 21 episode of Raw.

However, after Bayley cost Lyra her match against Iyo Sky this week on Raw by providing a distraction, it seems almost certain that there will be at least one more match between them.

articles.title: "Un Frankenstein": la insólita definición de Gustavo Alfaro sobre la Selección Colombia
articles.standfirst: Gustavo Alfaro sorprende y compara a la Selección Colombia con 'Frankenstein' previo al duelo
articles.summary: Gustavo Alfaro sorprende y compara a la Selección Colombia con 'Frankenstein' previo al duelo
articles.body: El director técnico de la Selección de Paraguay, Gustavo Alfaro, volvió a sorprender a la prensa deportiva con su habitual estilo conceptual para analizar a sus rivales. De cara al encuentro de fecha FIFA en Estados Unidos, el estratega argentino utilizó la analogía de la famosa criatura de Mary Shelley para calificar las múltiples facetas tácticas y variantes que presenta el equipo dirigido por Néstor Lorenzo. Lejos de tratarse de una descalificación o un dardo destructivo, la metáfora de Alfaro apuntó a elogiar la versatilidad del conjunto cafetero, destacando su capacidad para mutar según las exigencias del partido y el rival de turno. Durante sus declaraciones, el entrenador de la Albirroja explicó en detalle por qué considera a la 'Tricolor' una mezcla de varios estilos del continente sudamericano: "Para mí, es como una especie de Frankenstein si se quiere. Es una combinación de todos los partidos que jugamos. Tiene un poco de Uruguay, un poco de Ecuador y un poco de Bolivia, con lo de Colombia. En cuanto a la forma no hay que cambiar, pero luego hay que analizar detalles", señaló Alfaro. El análisis del DT argentino enfatiza que Colombia combina la intensidad física de selecciones como la uruguaya o ecuatoriana con la solidez estratégica y el talento técnico individual que históricamente ha caracterizado al fútbol colombiano. Alfaro también hizo referencia a las recientes presentaciones del combinado nacional, como el choque amistoso ante México, el cual destacó por su nivel de exigencia táctica y ritmo físico: El cruce entre Colombia y Paraguay suma un capítulo más a la paridad registrada en sus últimos enfrentamientos. En las Eliminatorias Sudamericanas, ambas escuadras protagonizaron un disputado encuentro en Barranquilla que finalizó 2-2, donde la Albirroja logró remontar una diferencia de dos goles. Con esta radiografía táctica, Gustavo Alfaro y Paraguay buscarán descifrar las diferentes piezas y variantes que componen el engranaje de Néstor Lorenzo en territorio estadounidense.

articles.summary: Se inicia en Melilla la II edición con un programa de competiciones hasta el 18 de que incluyen Campeonatos de Europa y de España y Copas de España
articles.body: La Ensenada de los Galápagos de Melilla, una cala espectacular bajo las imponentes murallas históricas de la ciudad autónoma, ha acogido este viernes la ceremonia de inauguración de los II Juegos del Agua, en un acto multitudinario que ha reunido a miles de personas y que ha convertido a Melilla en el gran escenario nacional de los Deportes acuáticos. Organizados por ADESP junto a 11 Federaciones Deportivas Españolas, los Juegos se celebran hasta el 18 de octubre con un programa que incluye Campeonatos de Europa, Campeonatos y Copas de España, además de exhibiciones. El momento culminante de la ceremonia ha sido la exhibición de Flyski, una espectacular disciplina que combina velocidad, acrobacia y vuelo sobre el agua, y que ha permitido al público disfrutar de una de las propuestas más llamativas del programa. La demostración ha puesto de manifiesto la vocación de los Juegos del Agua de acercar al público modalidades deportivas diversas y ofrecer una experiencia que vaya más allá de la competición. El acto ha contado con la presencia del Presidente de la Ciudad Autónoma de Melilla, Juan José Imbroda, y del presidente de ADESP, José Hidalgo, además de representantes de las Federaciones participantes y de las instituciones vinculadas al proyecto. Uno de los momentos más emotivos ha sido el homenaje a la ciudad de Ceuta, como gesto de solidaridad ante la grave crisis que está viviendo la otra ciudad española al norte de África. En la inauguración han participado los campeones mundiales Mario Mola -tres veces campeón del mundo de triatlón- e Iballa Ruano -diez títulos mundiales de windsurf-, y la ceremonia ha servido también para escenificar el relevo entre sedes. Representantes del Gobierno de la Región de Murcia, anfitriona de la primera edición de los Juegos del Agua, han participado en el acto y han entregado el testigo a Melilla, que toma ahora el relevo para dar continuidad a un proyecto que une competición, promoción territorial y colaboración entre Federaciones e instituciones. Con esta ceremonia, Melilla inicia oficialmente tres semanas de actividad deportiva en seis escenarios de la ciudad, gracias a la implicación de las Federaciones Españolas de natación, surfing, vela, triatlón, piragüismo, pesca, salvamento y socorrismo, pentatlón moderno, actividades subacuáticas, motonáutica y esquí náutico

articles.title: Luke Littler: World No 1 to headline World Youth Championships with chance to reach final at Minehead
articles.summary: Luke Littler will compete at the 2026 World Youth Championships but reigning champ Gian van Veen will not attend in the final year he is eligible; you can watch the conclusion of the World Grand Prix Darts live on Sky Sports this weekend
articles.body:
The full 128-player field for this year's showpiece will be finalised following the conclusion of the Development Tour season this weekend, with Events 21-24 taking place in Wigan on October 3-4.

The 2026 World Youth Championship will see the round-robin phase and the knockout phase from the last 64 down to the semi-finals staged on Monday October 5 at the Robin Park Leisure Centre.

Littler, who withdrew from Players Championship 29 and 30 after his defeat at the World Series Finals in Amsterdam effectively ended his chances of qualifying for the finals in Minehead in November, but he could still play at the venue.

The final will be held on Sunday November 29 at Butlin's Minehead Resort during the Ladbrokes Players Championship Finals, with a boosted top prize of £15,000 also on offer.

The 128-player line-up will include all age-qualified PDC Tour Card Holders who have accepted the invitation to compete and 26 international representatives, with the remaining places set to be filled from the final Development Tour Rankings.

The group stage sees the players split into 32 groups of four, with one seed per group for the round-robin action - with seedings based on the PDC Werner Rankings Ladder and then the Development Tour Rankings.

The top two players in each group will subsequently progress to the knockout stages, which begin from the last 64 onwards.

World Champion Littler - who lifted the World Youth Championship in 2023 - will be the top seed given his status as world No 1, ahead of Poland's Sebastian Bialecki and Ireland's Keane Barry.

Jurjen van der Velde - the 2024 runner-up - will also return alongside the likes of Cam Crabtree, Charlie Manby, Owen Bates and Czechia's Adam Gawlas.

The field also includes 16-year-old Lewis Cook from the JDC circuit - along with fellow stars Kaya Baysal, Archie Self and Ben Townley who have stepped up to the Development Tour this year - with Eleanor Cairns and Kyana Frauenfelder featuring from the PDC Women's Series rankings.

Reigning two-time champion Gian van Veen will not return to defend his title while Beau Greaves - runner-up to Van Veen 12 months ago - and Yorick Hofkens have also chosen not to compete in Monday's event.

The Winmau World Youth Championship will begin from 11.30am on Monday at the Robin Park Leisure Centre, with group games being played over the best of nine legs.

The top two players from each group will then advance to the last 64, which will be contested in a knockout format over the best of 11 legs.

articles.summary: These days, life after a great career has taken his serial entrepreneur mindset up a notch
articles.body:
Vernon Davis is widely considered one of the greatest tight ends in NFL history. These days, life after a great career has taken his serial entrepreneur mindset up a notch. From building a restaurant empire to acting and working with names like Morgan Freeman and Bruce Willis, to producing, learning musical instruments, and pursuing every creative outlet in between.

Davis recently sat down with Josh Petry of the Hoodie Chroniclez Podcast on YouTube to discuss his journey and a certain infamous incident involving former 49ers head coach Mike Singletary. For context, in October 2008, Singletary grew frustrated with Vernon Davis' lack of effort. During a game in which he sent Davis to the locker room, it ultimately affected Davis' career and became a turning point.

Davis was asked how he turned a moment of anger into something positive in his career. He would say, "Every young guy that comes into the league is going to go through some trial and error, different phases of their career where they're trying to find themselves, and I think for me, as a young man coming into the league, I was trying to find myself and figure it out."

Davis would also say, "A guy like Mike Singletary was essential for me because he helped me figure it out and find that lane that I was looking for. The biggest thing that I wanted was to be a leader on the team that I was playing on, and that was the San Francisco 49ers . He helped me turn that thing around and be everything that they wanted me to be."

articles.title: Ex-Toronto Blue Jays All-Star Still Owed $46 Million By Current MLB Team
articles.summary: A former Toronto Blue Jays All-Star is still owed $46 million by the New York Mets. He spent one year in Toronto. The post Ex-Toronto Blue Jays All-Star Stil...
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays didn't make the playoffs this year after finishing the season in last place in the American League East with a 79-83 record.

With Toronto's season over, let's take a look at a former Blue Jays All-Star who is still owed a lot of money by his current team.

Ex-Blue Jays All-Star Still Owed $46 Million By Mets

Semien spent the first two seasons of his MLB career (2013-14) with the Chicago White Sox.

The White Sox traded him to the Oakland Athletics after the 2014 season.

Semien played for Oakland through 2020. After the 2020 season, he signed a one-year, $18 million deal with the Blue Jays.

After his lone season with the Blue Jays, Semien signed a seven-year, $175 million contract with the Texas Rangers.

With Texas, Semien made two All-Star Teams and won the 2023 World Series.

The Rangers traded Semien to the New York Mets after the 2025 season. Texas received outfielder Brandon Nimmo in return.

Semien struggled in his first year with the Mets, posting 0.5 bWAR and a .215/.280/.340 slash line over 139 games.

Semien is under team control through the 2028 season. The Mets owe him $26 million in 2027 and $20 million in 2028.

Looking At Marcus Semien's Time With Toronto

Semien had a brief but memorable stint with the Blue Jays.

In his lone season with Toronto, Semien made his first All-Star Team.

He posted 7.1 bWAR and a .265/.334/.538 slash line with a career-best 45 home runs and 102 RBI over 162 games with Toronto in 2021.

He also won a Gold Glove and a Silver Slugger in his only year with the Blue Jays. He finished third in American League MVP voting that season.

articles.title: Q&A with Alabama beat writer Nick Kelly
articles.summary: No. 16 Mississippi State will host No. 7 Alabama on Saturday at 11 a.m.with ABC broadcasting the contest. To preview the matchup, the Daily Journal caught up...
articles.body:
No. 16 Mississippi State will host No. 7 Alabama on Saturday at 11 a.m.with ABC broadcasting the contest.

To preview the matchup, the Daily Journal caught up with Nick Kelly of al.com to discuss the upcoming game.

What are some of your biggest thoughts on how the season's gone for Alabama so far?

There have been some bumps along the way, but hey, 4-0 you'll take, and the schedule has kind of favored them well in terms of, "Hey, you kind of, not necessarily easier games, but you've got some easier games" where you're not playing your first SEC opponent being Georgia, like they had the last two years, and you're not going on the road against a Power 4 opponent in the first game, like they did last year. I think the schedule is set up favorably, almost a little preseason-like, if you will, which is kind of nice because you can just really work out your kinks and really just get to a point where you can see what you have, what you don't have, what your strengths are, where you need to work on things, and luckily the mistakes they've had have not cost them a victory, which is the best kind of learning experience, and so I think that helps. They now have this kind of murderers' row for ranked teams over the next five games.

Talk about how exactly Kalen DeBoer and Ryan Grubbs' offense works and how Keelon Russell brings it to its full potential.

I think the biggest word that comes to mind is "aggressive," and they will get after defenses. They like to push things. They like to go for it on fourth downs that make sense. They get after it, and I think Keelon fits their offense well, fits that mindset well because he's a player that gets after it. He'll make you pay with his arm or his legs, whatever makes sense. I think they like to have an RPO element that they maybe haven't had in recent years as much, but Keelon can bring that, and he's been working on that. He's not perfect at it. There've been some hiccups, but he can certainly be that type of quarterback. He's so talented, though, I don't care what your offense is. They can pretty much make him work. Meaning, you can find a way to use him that suits him well, even if he has to modify your offense. It's a nice marriage so far.

The run game was a point of emphasis in that it wasn't really where it needed to be last season. So far, do you feel like the run game is where it needs to be? Why or why not?

I think it is heading the right direction. Now we haven't seen it against better or high-level opponents, so I don't know if we can say that, "Hey, it's fixed. It's back," but I think you feel encouraged about it, considering they've been able to lean on teams and essentially make life difficult for teams late as the game's gone on. Kentucky, Florida State, the run game in both games, as the game went on, just was overwhelming. I think for both defenses. You feel good about the freshman running backs that they added, E.J. Crowell and Trae'shawn Brown, what they can bring. I mean, they haven't reached their potential yet by any means, and yet they've been really nice pieces for them in that attack. And then Daniel Hill, the Mississippi native, has taken his game to a new level this season. It's a group that I think is headed in the right direction. But again, there's kind of a cautious optimism in terms of once they face better opponents, we'll really get a feel.

What has stood out to you about the defense so far?

The front seven, I think, has been impressive, and we'd heard a lot of good optimism and buzz about some of the additions they made up front, like Devan Thompkins from Southern Cal, or you look at guys like Caleb Woodson for Virginia Tech. Of course, they added a familiar name for Mississippi State fans, Kedrick Bingley-Jones, who is a veteran guy for the rotation on the defensive line. So you knew that they were adding some pieces, but you didn't know how it would quite fit or how well it would go. And so far, it's been impressive. I mean, Devan Thompkins has been probably their biggest addition so far this season defensively. He's been a true difference maker up front. He can rush up the middle, off the edge, and he's a problem. He leads them in sacks, and he's tied for the lead in pressures. I think that's been an encouraging sign. Linebacker-wise, they've been strong considering they've almost hit reset in the middle with the inside linebackers. They unfortunately are without a couple of solid players off the edge right now in Desmond Umeozulu and Justin Hill, who are dealing with injuries, so that could hurt them in terms of the depth and just setting the edge and things like that, but you like that. The secondary was the most experienced and the most proven commodity, and there's a lot of talent there. It's been inconsistent so far, at least from a guy or two. I think that a couple guys need to just play better, and I do think that you still feel good about it, just because there is so much experience there and so much talent there, but there have been a few early busts in coverage or a few mistakes and some things that they want to keep smoothing out.

What are the expectations for Kalen DeBoer this season and how do they apply to this game?

Yeah, that's a good question. I would say the expectations are that he keeps improving on where they were, what they were doing last year. So that means, "Hey, make the playoff again," and ideally you can make it farther in the playoff. And past that, it's, "Hey, don't lose to the teams you're supposed to beat, and don't get blown out." Those are two things that have happened in the first two years of Kalen DeBoer prior to this year that Alabama fans aren't terribly used to, and it doesn't sit well with them, and so I think that's what progress looks like this year. Everyone obviously says that, "Hey, it's natty or bust every year," and it is to an extent. But I think realistically, as long as he's showing improvement, I think that will satisfy a lot of a lot of people in Tuscaloosa. How that applies to this game, before the season started, I would have said, "Well, it's avoiding a loss here because this could be a trap game." But Mississippi State seems pretty good, and this is a ranked matchup now, so I don't know if that quite fits that bill in terms of a trap game any more. Alabama is favored, I believe, but still not … if they lose this game, it won't be like, "Oh my gosh, the world's over" necessarily. It won't sit well. Alabama fans don't like to lose any game, but yeah, I don't know how it'll be viewed. It honestly could just be an important résumé piece for DeBoer and this team to make the playoff.

When you look at the matchup between these teams, where might you see advantages for Alabama and where might you see them for Mississippi State?

I would say Alabama's run defense has been good and could have a slight edge over Mississippi State's rushing attack, even though I think Fluff Bothwell is a really good player. So that's where I'm fascinated to see who wins that matchup. Maybe Alabama's secondary has a slight – I just feel like there's so many areas of this matchup that aren't a clear.. "Hey,, you feel way better about this group than that group." I know it's not a great answer, but I think … I'll say this: I think the fronts of Alabama, both defensively and offensively, could have an advantage, just in terms of talent and maybe size or strength. Again, I haven't seen Mississippi State, I do know that Alabama is much better in the trenches than they were a year ago. So, how Mississippi State handles that will be interesting and might be difficult.

What is an X-factor that might not be getting talked about as much that you feel like could make a huge impact on this game?

I think it's the two rushing attacks. We're talking so much about the quarterbacks, and for good reason. They're both exciting players and maybe two of the best in the country, but we haven't been talking as much about the rushing attacks, where as Alabama has had more success on the ground, and, again, Mississippi State with Fluff, I certainly like what they've been able to do there at times. I think that whoever wins the battle of the rushing attacks might actually have the edge here because ideally you're not giving the other offense the ball too much. You're holding onto it as long as you can so that you don't have to worry about getting beat by the quarterback. I think that could ultimately determine more than we've been talking about.

articles.title: Jalen Duren Returns to Pistons Facility, Bickerstaff Reacts
articles.summary: Jalen Duren is back at the Pistons facility, and JB Bickerstaff says he is in great shape. #Pistons
articles.body:
Jalen Duren signed his five-year, $200 million contract on Thursday right before the midnight deadline. Duren is only 22 years old and played in 70 games last season for the Detroit Pistons . He averaged 19.5 points per game, 10.5 rebounds per game, 2.0 assists per game, 0.8 blocks per game, and 0.8 steals per game.

Duren was back at the practice facility on Friday for Detroit. Head coach JB Bickerstaff is no doubt happy to have him back with the team.

Detroit Pistons Head Coach JB Bickerstaff comments on Jalen Duren returning to the facility

Pistons reporter Eric Woodyard relayed Bickerstaff's read on the return: Duren is in great shape, but the Pistons still have to sort out his ramp-up period before he hits the floor.

"We'll take our time figuring it out and we will go from there," Bickerstaff said.

Detroit will begin the season on Tuesday, Oct. 20 against the Boston Celtics with tip-off scheduled for 3 p.m. ET at Little Caesars Arena. Hopefully, Duren is up to speed by then and ready to go.

Jackson, who attends Bonney Lake High School in Bonney Lake, Washington, chose the Hoosiers over offers from Kansas, Cal, UNC and Big Ten rival USC, among others. She ranks in as the 20th highest-rated prospect in ESPN's SC Next 100 and joins Brookeslee Colvin and Finley Parker in Indiana's 2027 class.

She averaged 14.6 points and 14.8 rebounds per game as a junior in 2025-26 with her recruiting star skyrocketing. Standing at 6'4", she can get to her spots and score around the basket while seeing the floor well and fascilitating the offense as a passer.

articles.title: “A Little Bit Nasty”: Chiefs LB Fires Up Raiders Rivalry, Says KC Must “Bring That” Hate
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs and Las Vegas Raiders have been playing each other for more than six decades, but Sunday’s matchup feels different. Both teams are 3-0...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs and Las Vegas Raiders have been playing each other for more than six decades, but Sunday's matchup feels different. Both teams are 3-0, and the winner will leave Las Vegas alone atop the AFC West. The Raiders are also playing at home, where they have won their first three games of the season.

Kansas City has owned much of this rivalry in recent years. That makes Las Vegas' perfect start more important because the Raiders now have a chance to put pressure on the team that has controlled the division for so long.

Chiefs LB says the rivalry has turned "a little bit nasty"

Drue Tranquill was asked about the mood around the Chiefs-Raiders rivalry during the week. He said there is more edge to these games and made it clear that Kansas City expects a physical battle.

"It feels like there's more of that hate, if you will," Tranquill said . "It's a little bit nasty, a little bit tough. We'll have to bring that."

His comments make sense because of the current standings. The Chiefs are 3-0 after beating Denver, Indianapolis, and Miami. The Raiders are also 3-0 after wins against Miami, the Chargers, and New Orleans. Both teams are undefeated before they play each other for the first time this season.

Las Vegas is playing great defense too. The Raiders have 10 sacks and four interceptions in three games. Their plus-five turnover margin is the best in the NFL.

The Chiefs-Raiders rivalry has a long history

Kansas City has had the better side of this matchup for much of the Patrick Mahomes era. The Chiefs have won 16 of the last 20 meetings, although the Raiders won the most recent game, a 14-12 victory at home in last season's finale.

That history helps explain why this game means more than another early-season division matchup. Las Vegas has not entered a regular-season meeting with Kansas City at 3-0 or better on both sides before Sunday.

Mahomes also has another battle waiting for him in Maxx Crosby, who remains one of the Raiders' biggest defensive threats. Mahomes described their matchup as "pure football" and said the rivalry brings out the best in both players.

That gives Tranquill's comment more context. Kansas City is walking into a game that already has plenty of history behind it, but this time the Raiders are bringing an undefeated record with them.

The Chiefs linebacker knows the game could get physical. His message was simple. Kansas City has to be ready for it.

articles.title: Steelers Rookie Opens Up on First Career Interception
articles.summary: CLEVELAND — Pittsburgh Steelers rookie safety Robert Spears-Jennings was one of the few bright spots from Thursday night’s loss to […]
articles.body:
CLEVELAND — Pittsburgh Steelers rookie safety Robert Spears-Jennings was one of the few bright spots from Thursday night's loss to the Cleveland Browns.

Spears-Jennings, who replaced veteran Rayshawn Jenkins in the first half, recorded his first career interception in the third quarter. The Oklahoma product high-pointed a tipped pass with an assist from Jack Sawyer.

"It feels good. I mean, thankful for the opportunity," Spears-Jennings said about his first career INT.

Spears-Jennings said he realized the ball was coming when Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston's eyes got big.

"I was like, OK, the ball's coming. Ball in the air, I got to go get it," he said.

Spears-Jennings' interception initially got negated, as Daylen Everette was called for defensive pass interference. Mike McCarthy challenged the ruling since Sawyer tipped the pass, which makes interference a non-issue. The officials overturned the call on the field, giving Spears-Jennings his first career INT.

"I didn't know. I was talking with the refs," Spears-Jennings said when asked about the review process. "Once they clarified it, I felt good about myself."

Rooks first 🔒 @RobertJ3nnings 📲 Stream on NFL+: pic.twitter.com/hQo7d7wrYb — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) October 2, 2026

Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) October 2, 2026

Jenkins appeared to be the culprit behind another busted coverage that went for a 60-yard gain down the sideline, the coaching staff elected to bench him for the remainder of the contest.

To say the least, it was a brutal night for Jenkins. Spears-Jennings could be the starter moving forward. DeShon Elliott (hamstring), who is currently on the PUP list, is eligible to return in Week 5, however.

Getting Elliott back would be a big boost for the Steelers' ailing secondary. Spears-Jennings showed that he could be a starter on Thursday night, though. The rookie certainly turned heads.

Alan Saunders and Brendan Howe provided reporting from Cleveland.

articles.title: Tottenham Hotspur are in the race to sign Bayern Munich defender
articles.summary: Tottenham Transfer News: Kim Min-jae Interest Grows as Bayern Munich Weigh SaleTottenham’s search for defensive authority could yet lead them back towards Ki...
articles.body:
Tottenham Transfer News: Kim Min-jae Interest Grows as Bayern Munich Weigh Sale

Tottenham's search for defensive authority could yet lead them back towards Kim Min-jae, with TeamTalk reporting that Bayern Munich are prepared to consider a sale if the conditions are right. The South Korea international remains under contract until 2028, yet his place in the pecking order has shifted and that has naturally alerted a number of clubs.

The central detail is clear. Bayern are not actively forcing him out, but there is now a realistic scenario in which movement becomes possible. As reported, Bayern are "open to selling the South Korean international if the right offer arrives", a line that immediately sharpens attention around Tottenham, Aston Villa and several major Italian sides.

For Spurs, the timing is significant. A defender of this calibre, age and experience would usually command a much wider race, yet TeamTalk state that "a bid of £30million will be enough to secure Min-jae's signature next summer". In a market where proven centre-backs often cost far more, that figure stands out.

There is important context around Bayern's thinking. Kim, now 29, has "slipped to third choice behind Dayot Upamecano and Jonathan Tah under Vincent Kompany". That reduced status does not mean an immediate departure is imminent, because "Nothing is advanced" and the player is "content to stay and comfortable with his current squad role, even if starts are limited."

That said, clubs have not walked away. Tottenham, Aston Villa and AC Milan "all made contact over him in the summer without lodging a formal bid, and all three remain interested". Juventus are also "among the sides monitoring his situation", which points to a competitive market once Bayern's direction becomes clearer.

There is also a scheduling element to this story. A winter move is possible in theory, but TeamTalk suggest "A January move is regarded as more unlikely, the more realistic window is next summer". From Bayern's perspective, that makes sense if they still want to preserve value while reshaping the defence.

Tottenham and Aston Villa Ready to Revisit

For Tottenham, Kim Min-jae ticks several boxes. He brings top-level European experience, physical authority and a profile already tested in high-pressure environments. The report points to "Premier League-ready experience and a proven profile" and references his title-winning impact at Napoli. That background is precisely why Spurs are watching closely.

Villa's interest adds another layer, especially given that Kim "turned down interest from Aston Villa and a tentative enquiry from Nottingham Forest" over the summer. Whether that changes next year may depend on role, European football and the clarity offered by Bayern.

One line matters above all: "it will also depend on whether the defender, for all his willingness to stay, is ultimately told he needs to find a new club". Until that point, this remains one to monitor rather than one nearing completion.

From a Tottenham supporter's perspective, this is exactly the kind of deal the club should be exploring. Kim Min-jae has presence, pedigree and the sort of calm authority Spurs have lacked far too often at the back. If the £30million figure is accurate, it feels like a rare opportunity to bring in a defender with elite-level experience for a fee that is relatively modest by modern standards.

The obvious concern is the wider state of the club. The report rightly points out that Tottenham's hopes "will of course depend on them staying in the Premier League", and that is the uncomfortable backdrop to everything at the moment. Any ambitious transfer plan becomes harder to execute when results are this poor and uncertainty surrounds the direction of the team.

Even so, this is where recruitment has to be brave and forward-looking. If Spurs believe Kim can transform the defence, they should position themselves early. Waiting for the perfect moment often means missing out. Villa, Milan and Juventus will not hang around if Bayern signal a clear willingness to do business.

There is also a personality question here. If Kim is "content to stay", Tottenham would need a compelling pitch around minutes, responsibility and the project ahead. That means clarity from the club hierarchy and from Roberto De Zerbi. Supporters would surely welcome a defender with Kim's level of experience, but they would also want reassurance that this would be part of a bigger reset, not a standalone move made in isolation.

On quality alone, this looks like a chase worth pursuing.

articles.title: Ohio State-Iowa, Penn State-Northwestern and more: Previewing Week 5 of Big Ten football
articles.summary: Ryan Day leads Ohio State into Kinnick Stadium and Northwestern looks to further derail Matt Campbell’s Penn State debut.
articles.body:
Our glorious *Midwestern-based college football conference is fully into conference play and we've got some interesting games to talk about this week and some… that are also happening, okay?

Without further ado, let's get into the Big Ten's Week 5 slate:

This is the week's top matchup that's absolutely worth tuning into if you're at all interested in the league.

No. 5 Ohio State Buckeyes at No. 14 Iowa Hawkeyes

Ohio State returns to Kinnick Stadium for the first time since losing 55-24 there to an unranked Iowa team, a loss that effectively ended the Buckeyes' National Championship aspirations in 2017. Nine years later, Ohio State will once again need to win to preserve their postseason hopes after having suffered a loss at Texas.

At No. 14 in this week's AP Poll, this isn't an Iowa team like 2017's that will catch people off guard. The Hawkeyes played an impressive four quarter game last week in Ann Arbor, winning on the final play to deal Michigan its first official loss of the season. Ohio State will be big favorites still, but there's no reason to count out this Iowa team with one upset under its belt already and a raucous home crowd behind it.

This is somewhere between the Game of the Week and The Rest. Definitely more interesting than most of the matchups but not as prominent as the top contest.

Penn State Nittany Lions at Northwestern Wildcats

Northwestern gave Indiana just about everything it could handle last Friday, coming oh so close to a statement win against a top-5 team on the road. The Wildcats will have another chance at a statement on Friday night, welcoming a Penn State team coming off of an upset home loss against Wisconsin choked away in the fourth quarter to spoil Matt Campbell's first homecoming, and potentially first season, in State College.

The Wildcats are feisty. Are they feisty enough to send the Nittany Lions into a spiral?

Here's a few other games worth a glance to see if anything interesting is going on.

Michigan Wolverines at Minnesota Golden Gophers

This one is interesting for watching Michigan's first season under Kyle Whittingham unfold. The Wolverines should have two losses already, one to Western Michigan to open the season and other to Iowa on last week's final play, instead holding just the latter. That win over Oklahoma isn't exactly aging well either.

Will Michigan spiral further? Or roll over Minnesota, which itself is coming off of a road upset at Washington?

Michigan State Spartans at Wisconsin Badgers

This one is here for a very simple reason: traditional Big Ten matchup between two teams coached by former linebackers. Who can out-tough the other?

This game could also give us a better idea of which direction these two programs are heading in. Wisconsin got a win over Penn State that could save the Luke Fickell era if they can build on that momentum and reach a bowl game. Michigan State has dropped two straight and will be looking to get back on track so as to not waste Pat Fitzgerald's first season at the helm.

Purdue Boilermakers at Illinois Fighting Illini

Well. This is a football game, for sure.

Purdue fans got to see their Illinois counterparts live out their dreams this week when the Fighting Illini parted ways with defensive coordinator Bobby Hauck just four games into the season. Both of these teams have poor defenses and, as a result, pass the ball quite a bit.

This will be like a taste of the old Big 12. All the offense, none of the defense. Well, maybe all of the offense. We'll see (or not, this is kind of a screen four in a multi-view type game)!

Washington Huskies at No. 18 USC Trojans

Both of these teams are coming off tough losses, with the Huskies falling the Minnesota and dropping out of the top 25 while USC got thumped by Dylan Raiola and Oregon. It's early enough in the season for either of these teams to be optimistic about getting their seasons back on track, but it starts with a win this week. A road win for Washington over a ranked team would surely get the Huskies back into the top 25, while a win over Washington would probably be USC's best win of the season so far.

I think this one matters more for USC, so I would expect them to respond. That said, the Oregon loss cast doubts on more than just this season for the Trojans, so it'll be interesting to see if Lincoln Riley still has the ability to rally his troops.
