articles.title: Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson ruled out for Dolphins game
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson will not play in Week 4 against the Miami Dolphins, coach Kevin O'Connell announced Friday.
articles.body:
Oct. 2 (UPI) -- Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson will not play in Week 4 against the Miami Dolphins, coach Kevin O'Connell announced Friday.

Jefferson, who hurt his ankle Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, did not practice this week. O'Connell told reporters that the Vikings will try to get Jefferson back into practice next week.

"He's definitely feeling better," O'Connell said. "I think we are encouraged about where he's at, but just couldn't get there."

Jefferson leads the Vikings with 13 catches, 179 receiving yards and two touchdowns this season. He drew 17 targets through the first three weeks of his 2026 campaign.

Tai Felton, Jeshaun Jones and Myles Price are the Vikings' backup wide receivers, behind Jefferson and fellow starters Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings.

Addison logged a game-high 90 yards and a score off five catches in the Vikings' 23-16 win Sunday in Tampa, Fla.

O'Connell said Friday that cornerback Charles Demmings and punter Brett Thorson, who sustained hamstring injuries, also are out for the Vikings' Week 4 meeting with the Dolphins.

The Vikings will promote punter Johnny Hekker to their active roster for Sunday's matchup, which will kick off at 4:05 p.m. EDT in Minneapolis.

articles.title: Dan Campbell: Brian Branch is close to returning
articles.summary: Lions safety Brian Branch is almost completely recovered from last year's torn Achilles tendon.
articles.body:
Lions safety Brian Branch is almost completely recovered from last year's torn Achilles tendon.

That's the word from Lions head coach Dan Campbell, who said today that Branch will return to the field soon.

"He's close. Yep, he's close. He's ready to go," Campbell said.

Campbell said Branch has been in his ear about how ready he feels to get back out there.

"Tired of listening to him — I mean that in a good way," Campbell said. "He's put in a ton of work and he looks really good. He's close."

Campbell did not say when Branch will return, but he could be activated from the physically unable to perform list as soon as next week, in time for the Lions' Week 5 game against the Cardinals.

articles.title: Seattle Mariners claim Michael Toglia off waivers from Cincinnati Reds
articles.summary: Toglia’s Reds career ends after 10 games and a busted shoulder.
articles.body:
The Michael Toglia Era in Cincinnati Reds history was short and sweet despite the man, who I'm sure is sweet enough, being anything but short.

The 6'5" former 1st round pick of the Colorado Rockies spent the 2026 season within the Reds organization, plying his trade almost exclusively with AAA Louisville. As the injuries and underperformance mounted at the big league level, however, the Reds turned to Toglia's prodigious power in August and he ultimately managed to play 10 games for them.

Curiously, the Reds decided to give him – at age 28 – his first ever career starts in LF during that run. Mostly a 1B by trade (with admittedly experience in RF), Toglia dislocated his right shoulder diving for a ball in LF in an August 21st game against the Arizona Diamondbacks that ended both his season and, as of today, his career with the Reds.

Toglia was claimed off waivers by the Seattle Mariners on Friday afternoon, adding yet another layer of Mariners/Reds personnel overlap during the last decade.

While Toglia went just 3 for 26 with a pair of walks and 12 Ks in his Reds career, there's plenty of pop in his bat that has played up elsewhere at times. That includes down at Louisville this past season as he socked 22 homers in 97 games for them, and he swatted 25 at the big league level with the Rockies as recently as 2024. So, this move does further dent the depth on the Reds roster, particularly in the power department (which is sorely lacking at just about every level at the moment).

The move means the Reds currently have 37 men on their 40-man roster, though Toglia was one of four Reds currently on the 60-day IL who'd need to be returned to the roster at season's end (with Hunter Greene, Spencer Steer, and Blake Dunn being the others).

articles.title: Braves will be without $3.5M All-Star for NLDS vs. Dodgers as starting pitching falters
articles.summary: The Atlanta Braves are already facing a huge concern with their starting pitching in the NLDS. It now seems as if a veteran will be returning like originally...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Braves will face the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLDS with a lot of questions surrounding their starting pitching. It is already a tough ask to go up against the Dodgers, but it is even tougher with an unclear pitching plan.

Atlanta suffered a major blow to its starting rotation during the final week of the regular season when Martín Pérez went down with an injury.

"The Braves' rotation depth was dealt another blow on Thursday, when it was learned that Martín Pérez will likely not be available during the first two rounds of the postseason. The Braves placed Pérez on the 15-day injured list with lower back inflammation," MLB.com's Mark Bowman wrote.

The veteran All-Star would be able to come back in Game 3 at the very earliest. Even that expectation would be very optimistic considering the injury is inflammation.

"Assuming Martin Perez's IL move is backdated to Monday, he wouldn't be eligible to return until Oct. 6 (NLDS Game 3). Weiss said he doesn't know if Elder will be available by the start of the IL. That's probably optimistic to think he could return before the NLCS," Bowman posted.

On Friday, Braves manager Walt Weiss met with the media to discuss the upcoming series against the Dodgers. It was there that he confirmed Pérez will not be back for the NLDS at all, as he is still getting over his injury.

"Walt Weiss said Lane Thomas is a possibility for this Division Series against the Dodgers. Bryce Elder and Martin Perez won't be on the roster. Both could be ready if the Braves advance to the NLCS," Bowman wrote.

Atlanta will now be without another starting pitcher in this series. The team is going to have to count on guys like AJ Smith-Shawver and likely JR Ritchie to really eat some innings in the first two games.

Pérez is on a $3.5 million contract with the Braves this season. It does hurt to lose Pérez, but if they can get past LA, they will certainly have him against whoever is in the NLCS. For all the factors included, it does hurt not to have Pérez on the roster for this huge series.
